title.zh: 卷八十下 文苑列傳
title.raw: 卷八十下 文苑列傳 Volume 80b: Biographies of Writers 2

sentences.zh: 张升字彦真，陈留尉氏人，富平侯放之孙也。

translations.literal: Zhang Sheng, courtesy name Yanzhen, was a man of Weishi in Chenliu, grandson of Marquis Fuping Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Sheng, whose courtesy name was Yanzhen, came from Weishi in Chenliu commandery; he was a grandson of Marquis Fuping Zhang Fang.

sentences.zh: 升少好学，多关览，而任情不羁。

translations.literal: Sheng in youth loved learning, read widely in many connections, yet followed his feelings and was unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he loved books and ranged through many fields, but he followed his moods and refused to be tamed.

sentences.zh: 其意相合者，则倾身交结，不问穷贱；

translations.literal: Where their intents matched, then he inclined his person to friendship, not asking whether they were destitute or base.
translations.idiomatic: When he found a kindred spirit he gave himself wholly to the bond, never asking whether the man was poor or lowborn.

sentences.zh: 如乖真志好者，虽王公大人，终不屈从。

translations.literal: If they deviated from true intent and likes, though kings and dukes, in the end he would not bow and follow.
translations.idiomatic: If someone's aims ran counter to his own, not even princes of the blood could make him bend.

sentences.zh: 常叹曰：“死生有命，富贵在天。

translations.literal: He often sighed, saying: "Death and life have their fate; wealth and honor lie with Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He used to sigh: "Life and death are fated; wealth and rank rest with Heaven.

sentences.zh: 其有知我，虽胡越可亲；

translations.literal: Those who know me—even Hu and Yue may be kin;
translations.idiomatic: Men who understand me may be as distant as the Hu and Yue tribes, yet they are kin.

sentences.zh: 苟不相识，从物何益？

translations.literal: if I do not know them, what use in piling up things?"
translations.idiomatic: If they do not know me, what good is a heap of possessions?"

sentences.zh: 仕郡为纲纪，以能出守外黄令。

translations.literal: He served in the commandery as chief clerk; because of ability he was sent out to hold the magistracy of Waihuang.
translations.idiomatic: He served his commandery as chief clerk, then for his competence was posted magistrate of Waihuang.

sentences.zh: 吏有受赇者，即论杀之。

translations.literal: When clerks accepted bribes, he immediately tried and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: Any clerk caught taking bribes he tried at once and put to death.

sentences.zh: 或讥：“升守领一时，何足趋明威戮乎？

translations.literal: Someone ridiculed: "Sheng's guarding the lead is only one season—why hurry to display severity and killing?"
translations.idiomatic: Critics said: "Your tenure is a single turn of the seasons—why rush to blood and terror?"

sentences.zh: ”对曰：“昔仲尼暂相，诛齐之侏儒，手足异门而出，故能威震强国，反其侵地。

translations.literal: He replied: "Formerly Zhongni was briefly minister and executed the dwarf performers of Qi; hands and feet went out different gates—thereby he could awe a mighty state and recover invaded territory.
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "Confucius held office only briefly, yet he executed Qi's dancing dwarfs and had their limbs dragged out separate gates—enough to overawe a great power and win back stolen land.

sentences.zh: 君子仕不为己，职思其忧，岂以久近而异其度哉？

translations.literal: The gentleman holds office not for himself; the duty is to think of its worries—how can long or short duration alter the measure?"
translations.idiomatic: A gentleman serves the public, not his purse; the charge is to shoulder its cares—why should the length of a posting change the rule?"

sentences.zh: ”遇党锢去官，后竟见诛，年四十九。

translations.literal: " He met the Partisan Prohibition and lost office; afterward in the end he was seen executed, age forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: The faction proscription stripped him of office; later he was put to death at forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 著贼、诔、颂、碑、书，凡六十篇。

translations.literal: What he authored—fu, dirges, odes, stelae, letters—totals sixty pieces.
translations.idiomatic: His writings—rhapsodies, laments, hymns, inscriptions, and letters—number sixty pieces.

sentences.zh: 赵壹字元叔，汉阳西县人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Yi, courtesy name Yuanshu, was a man of Xixian in Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yi, courtesy name Yuanshu, was a native of Xixian in Hanyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 体貌魁梧，身长九尺，美须豪眉，望之甚伟。

translations.literal: His frame was imposing; his body nine chi in height; he had a handsome beard and bold brows—looking at him he was very majestic.
translations.idiomatic: He was a giant of nine Han feet, with a noble beard and fierce brows—every inch the hero.

sentences.zh: 而恃才倨傲，为乡党所摈，乃作《解摈》。

translations.literal: Yet relying on talent he was arrogant and haughty; his village cohorts rejected him; therefore he composed "Relieving Rejection."
translations.idiomatic: Talent made him proud, and his neighbors shunned him; he answered with his essay "On Shaking Off Rejection."

sentences.zh: 后屡抵罪，几至死，友人救，得免。

translations.literal: Later repeatedly he touched crime and nearly died; friends rescued him and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: He later fell afoul of the law more than once and nearly perished; friends ransomed him back to life.

sentences.zh: 壹乃贻书谢恩曰：

translations.literal: Yi then sent a letter thanking kindness, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He then wrote a letter of thanks that began:

sentences.zh: 昔原大夫赎桑下绝气，传称其仁；

translations.literal: Anciently Counselor Zhao Dun ransomed a man dying breathless under a mulberry—the tradition praises his benevolence;
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Zhao Dun redeemed a starving man beneath a mulberry—the chronicles praise his kindness;

sentences.zh: 秦越人还虢太子结脉，世著其神。

translations.literal: Qin Yueren restored the heir of Guo's knotted pulse—the age records his spiritlike skill.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Que of Qin restarted the crown prince of Guo's halted pulse—the world calls that divine healing.

sentences.zh: 设曩之二人不遭仁遇神，则结绝之气竭矣。

translations.literal: Suppose those two men had not encountered benevolence and spirit—then the breath of knotted severance would have been exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Had those two patients missed such rescuers, the last breath would have left their throats.

sentences.zh: 然而□脯出乎车軨，针石运乎手爪。

translations.literal: Yet dried meat came from the chariot crossbar; needles and stones moved in hands and claws.
translations.idiomatic: Yet dried meat was handed from the chariot rail, needles and lancets worked in human hands.

sentences.zh: 今所赖者，非直车軨之糒脯，手爪之针石也。

translations.literal: What I now rely on is not merely the dried rations of the chariot rail, nor merely the needle-stone of hand and claw.
translations.idiomatic: What I lean on today is no mere trail ration or bedside lancet.

sentences.zh: 乃收之于斗极，还之于司命，使干皮复含血，枯骨复被肉，允所谓遭仁遇神，真所宜传而著之。

translations.literal: Rather you gathered me at the Dipper's Pivot, returned me at the Director of Fate, made withered skin again hold blood, dead bones again wear flesh—this is truly what is called meeting benevolence and encountering spirit, truly what ought to be transmitted and made illustrious.
translations.idiomatic: You plucked me from the Pole Star, handed me back to the Director of Fate—withered hide drinks blood again, dry bones take flesh—this is the "benevolence and spirit" the ages should record.

sentences.zh: 余畏禁，不敢班班显言，窃为《穷鸟赋》一篇。

translations.literal: I fear prohibition and dare not speak in ordered detail; privately I have made one piece, "Rhapsody on the Destitute Bird."
translations.idiomatic: I dare not speak openly under the ban; I have instead drafted a "Rhapsody on the Destitute Bird."

sentences.zh: 其辞曰：

translations.literal: Its wording says:
translations.idiomatic: The text runs:

sentences.zh: 有一穷鸟，戢翼原野。

translations.literal: There was a destitute bird, folding wings on the wild plain.
translations.idiomatic: There was a starving bird, wings folded on the waste.

sentences.zh: 毕网加上，机□在下，前见苍隼，后见驱者，缴弹张右，羿子彀左，飞丸激矢，交集于我。

translations.literal: Closing nets above, spring-traps below; ahead he saw the grey falcon, behind the beaters; bowstrings and pellets spread to the right, Yi's archer's bow drawn to the left; flying pellets and swift arrows converged on me.
translations.idiomatic: Nets roofed the sky, snares waited below; a goshawk hung ahead, beaters closed from behind; slings and bolts to the right, the archer Yi's bow to the left—shot and shaft rained on me at once.

sentences.zh: 思飞不得，欲鸣不可，举头畏触，摇足恐堕。

translations.literal: It wished to fly but could not, wished to cry but could not; lifting its head feared collision, moving its feet feared falling.
translations.idiomatic: It could neither fly nor cry; lifting its head risked a blow, shifting a foot risked the drop.

sentences.zh: 内独怖急，乍冰乍火。

translations.literal: Within alone terrified and urgent, now ice now fire.
translations.idiomatic: Inside it burned and froze by turns with terror.

sentences.zh: 幸赖大贤，我矜我怜，昔济我南，今振我西。

translations.literal: Luckily relying on a great worthy who pitied me, once aided me south, now rouses me west.
translations.idiomatic: A great man pitied me—once he saved me in the south, now he lifts me in the west.

sentences.zh: 鸟也虽顽，犹识密思。

translations.literal: Though the bird is stupid, it still knows secret kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Dull as a bird is, it knows hidden grace.

sentences.zh: 内以书心，外用告天。

translations.literal: Within it writes on the heart; without it announces to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: It inscribes gratitude on the heart and cries it to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 天乎祚贤，归贤永年，且公且侯，子了孙孙。

translations.literal: O Heaven bless the worthy, return the worthy long years—both duke and marquis, sons and grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: May Heaven bless that worthy, grant him long life, raise him duke and marquis, and crown his sons and grandsons.

sentences.zh: 又作《刺世疾邪赋》，以舒其怨愤。

translations.literal: Again he composed "Rhapsody Stabbing the Age and Hating Evil" to vent his resentment and fury.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote the "Rhapsody on Vilifying the Age and Detesting Villainy" to vent his rage.

sentences.zh: 曰：

translations.literal: It says:
translations.idiomatic: It says:

sentences.zh: 伊五帝之不同礼，三王亦又不同乐，数极自然变化，非是故相反驳。

translations.literal: Those Five Theodarchs had not the same rites; the Three Kings likewise had not the same music—number reaches its limit and nature transforms; it is not that they therefore contrary refuted each other.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Thearchs kept different rites, the Three Kings different music—when a cycle runs its course, things change of themselves; they were not contradicting one another for sport.

sentences.zh: 德政不能救世混乱，赏罚岂足惩时清浊？

translations.literal: Virtuous government cannot rescue the age from chaos; how could reward and punishment suffice to chastise the age's clarity and turbidity?
translations.idiomatic: Good government cannot cure an age gone mad; rewards and fines will not scour its clean and foul.

sentences.zh: 春秋时祸败之始，战国愈复增其荼毒。

translations.literal: Spring and Autumn was the start of disaster and ruin; Warring States again increased its bitter poison.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn era opened the road to ruin; the Warring States poured poison on the wound.

sentences.zh: 秦、汉无以相逾越，乃更加其怨酷。

translations.literal: Qin and Han could not surpass each other, yet each added its resentful cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Qin and Han strove to outdo one another only in spite and cruelty.

sentences.zh: 宁计生民之命，唯利己而自足。

translations.literal: They would not reckon the life of the people—only profit self and be self-satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: They never weighed the people's lives—only fattened themselves and called it enough.

sentences.zh: 于兹迄今，情伪万方。

translations.literal: From then to now, feeling and sham are in myriad ways.
translations.idiomatic: From that hour to this, truth and sham wear ten thousand masks.

sentences.zh: 佞谄日炽，刚克消亡。

translations.literal: Flattery blazes daily; the upright and able perish.
translations.idiomatic: Sycophancy burns hotter each day; the straight and strong are snuffed out.

sentences.zh: 舐痔结驷，正色徒行。

translations.literal: Those who lick hemorrhoids hitch four-horse teams; men of correct countenance go on foot.
translations.idiomatic: The flatterer rides four-in-hand; the honest man walks.

sentences.zh: 妪□禹名势，抚拍豪强。

translations.literal: Old women steal Yu's name for power, stroke and pat the mighty.
translations.idiomatic: Harridans borrow the great name of Yu to fawn on the powerful.

sentences.zh: 偃蹇反俗，立致咎殃。

translations.literal: Lofty and contrary to custom—at once they incur blame and disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Stand aloof from the crowd and trouble finds you at once.

sentences.zh: 捷慑逐物，日富月昌。

translations.literal: Nimble timidity chases things—daily richer, monthly thriving.
translations.idiomatic: The craven time-server chases every wind—richer each day, fatter each month.

sentences.zh: 浑然同惑，孰温孰凉？

translations.literal: Muddled in the same delusion—who is warm, who is cool?
translations.idiomatic: The mob shares one stupidity—who can tell warmth from chill?

sentences.zh: 邪夫显进，直士幽藏。

translations.literal: Evil men advance in plain sight; straight men hide away.
translations.idiomatic: Villains stride the halls; the upright hide in the dark.

sentences.zh: 原斯瘼之攸兴，实执政之匪贤。

translations.literal: Track this malady's arising—in truth the rulers are not worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Trace this sickness to its root—the men at the helm are not worthies.

sentences.zh: 女谒掩其视听兮，近习秉其威权。

translations.literal: Women's pleas cover their ears and eyes; favorites grasp their awesome power.
translations.idiomatic: Palace whispers seal their ears and eyes; favorites clutch the awful seal.

sentences.zh: 所好则钻皮出其毛羽，所恶则洗垢求其瘢痕。

translations.literal: What they like—they drill the skin to bring out feathers; what they hate—they wash the stain seeking scars.
translations.idiomatic: What they favor grows feathers from bare skin; what they hate is scrubbed until a scar appears.

sentences.zh: 虽欲谒诚而尽忠，路绝嶮而靡缘。

translations.literal: Though one wish to exhaust sincerity and loyalty, the road is cut off sheer and without path.
translations.idiomatic: Though you would pour out every loyal drop, the road is a cliff without a ledge.

sentences.zh: 九重既不可启，又群吠之狺狺。

translations.literal: The nine-fold gates cannot be opened; moreover a pack yaps and yaps.
translations.idiomatic: The nine inner gates stay barred; a kennel of curs snarls beyond.

sentences.zh: 安危于于旦夕，肆嗜欲于目前。

translations.literal: Safety and peril hang between dawn and dusk; they indulge appetites before their eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Life or death hangs between sunrise and dusk, yet they gorge their lusts while they can.

sentences.zh: 奚异涉海之失舵，积薪而待燃？

translations.literal: How does it differ from crossing the sea having lost the helm, heaping fuel waiting for the blaze?
translations.idiomatic: What is that but sailing the deep without a rudder or stacking kindling for the spark?

sentences.zh: 荣纳由于闪揄，孰知辩其蚩妍？

translations.literal: Glory and intake come from shifty sidling—who can tell ugly from fair?
translations.idiomatic: Rank and salary go to the sidling sneak—who can tell beauty from filth?

sentences.zh: 故法禁屈挠干势族，恩泽不逮于单门。

translations.literal: Therefore the law's prohibitions bend before powerful clans; favor's dew does not reach single-door homes.
translations.idiomatic: So the statutes buckle before great houses, while mercy never drips on the poor lone door.

sentences.zh: 宁饥寒于尧、舜之荒岁兮，不饱暖于当今之丰年。

translations.literal: Better hunger and cold in a lean year of Yao and Shun than glut and warmth in this age's fat year.
translations.idiomatic: Better shiver in a bad year of Yao and Shun than feast in the fat years of today.

sentences.zh: 乘理虽死而非亡，违义虽生而匪存。

translations.literal: Riding principle, though dead, is not gone; betraying right, though alive, is not existing.
translations.idiomatic: Cling to the right and death cannot unmake you; betray it and life is a walking corpse.

sentences.zh: 有秦客者，乃为诗曰：“河清不可俟，人命不可延。

translations.literal: A guest from Qin then made a poem: "The river cannot be waited clear; man's fate cannot be extended.
translations.idiomatic: A western visitor sang: "You cannot wait for the Yellow River to run clear; you cannot bargain with fate for more years.

sentences.zh: 顺风激靡草，富贵者称贤。

translations.literal: Following the wind it whips withered grass—rich and noble are called worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Wind bends the dry grass—so the rich pass for sages.

sentences.zh: 文籍虽满腹，不如一囊钱。

translations.literal: Though texts fill the belly, they are not worth one purse of cash.
translations.idiomatic: A bellyful of books is worth less than a purse of cash.

sentences.zh: 伊优北堂上，抗脏倚门边。

translations.literal: The obsequious throng the north hall; the upright are left by the gate.
translations.idiomatic: The yes-man struts the north hall; the straight man leans on the gate.

sentences.zh: 鲁生闻此辞，系而作歌曰：势家多所宜，咳唾自成珠。

translations.literal: The man of Lu hearing these words, continued and composed a song: "Powerful families are suited in everything; cough and spit turn to pearls.
translations.idiomatic: A man of Lu heard the verse and sang back: "Great houses can do no wrong—spittle turns to pearls.

sentences.zh: 被褐怀金玉，兰蕙化为刍。

translations.literal: Clad in coarser cloth yet holding jade and gold—orchid and iris turn to fodder.
translations.idiomatic: The poor may carry jade in the heart, yet orchid grace is chewed like hay.

sentences.zh: 贤者虽独悟，所困在群愚。

translations.literal: Though the worthy alone awakens, he is trapped among the herd of fools.
translations.idiomatic: The sage may wake alone, but the mob of fools pens him in.

sentences.zh: 且各守尔分，勿复空驰驱。

translations.literal: For now each keep your lot—do not again vainly career.
translations.idiomatic: Each of you keep your station—do not waste breath in useless striving.

sentences.zh: 哀哉复哀哉，此是命矣夫！

translations.literal: Alas, alas again—this is fate!"
translations.idiomatic: Alas, alas—this is Heaven's sentence!"

sentences.zh: 光和元年，举郡上计，到京师。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guanghe, raised as the commandery's capital-clerk reporter, he arrived at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Guanghe 1 the commandery sent him up as chief clerk; he reached Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 是时，司徒袁逢受计，计吏数百人，皆拜伏庭中，莫敢仰视。

translations.literal: At that time Steward Yuan Feng received the accounts; several hundred clerks all bowed prostrate in the court, none daring look up.
translations.idiomatic: Steward Yuan Shou was receiving the year-end returns; hundreds of clerks lay face down in the yard, none daring lift his eyes.

sentences.zh: 壹独长揖而已。

translations.literal: Yi alone made a long bow-handshake salute, that was all.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yi alone gave the long crossbow salute and stood straight.

sentences.zh: 逢望而异之，令左右往让之，曰：“下郡计吏而揖三公，何也？

translations.literal: Feng saw him from afar and thought him strange, ordered attendants to rebuke him, saying: "A low commandery clerk bowing with hands to the Three Dukes—why?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuan watched from afar, startled, and sent aides to scold him: "Who is a back-country clerk to salute the Three Excellencies?"

sentences.zh: ”对曰：“昔郦食其长揖汉王，今揖三公，何遽怪哉？

translations.literal: He replied: "Long ago Li Yiji made a long bow to the King of Han; now I bow to the Three Dukes—how is that suddenly strange?"
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Li Yiji once gave Han Gaozu only a deep bow; I do the same for the Three Dukes—why the fuss?"

sentences.zh: ”逢则敛衽下堂，执其手，延置上坐，因问西方事，大悦，顾谓坐中曰：“此人汉阳赵元叔也。

translations.literal: Feng then gathered his lapels, stepped down the hall, grasped his hand, led him to the upper seat, asked him of western affairs, was greatly pleased, looked back to those seated: "This man is Zhao Yuanshu of Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan straightened his robe, came down the steps, took his hand, seated him above, questioned him on the west, and beamed: "This is Zhao Yuanshu of Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 朝臣莫有过之者，吾请为诸君分坐。

translations.literal: No court minister surpasses him—I request to yield my seat for you all."
translations.idiomatic: No man at court tops him—I will share my cushion with you all."

sentences.zh: ”坐者皆属观。

translations.literal: " Those seated all turned to watch.
translations.idiomatic: Every guest twisted round to stare.

sentences.zh: 既出，往造河南尹羊陟，不得见。

translations.literal: When he went out he went to call on Intendant of Henan Yang Zhi but could not get audience.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving the hall he called on Yang Zhi, intendant of Henan, and was turned away.

sentences.zh: 壹以公卿中非陟无足以托名者，乃日往到门，陟自强许通，尚卧未起。

translations.literal: Yi thought that among dukes none but Zhi sufficed to lodge his name; therefore day after day he went to the gate; Zhi finally forced himself to grant passage, was still in bed not risen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yi reckoned Yang Zhi the only minister worth a name, so he haunted the gate daily until Yang grudgingly admitted him—yet Yang still lay abed.

sentences.zh: 壹径入上堂，遂前临之，曰：“窃伏西州，承高风旧矣。

translations.literal: Yi went straight into the upper hall, stepped forward to his couch, saying: "I have lain hidden in the western province, long hearing your lofty wind."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yi walked straight to the inner chamber, stood over the couch, and said: "I have hidden in the western marches, yet long admired your high repute.

sentences.zh: 乃今方遇而忽然，奈何命也！

translations.literal: "Now I have just met you yet you are aloof—what can be done—fate!"
translations.idiomatic: Now we meet and you turn cold—what is left but fate?"

sentences.zh: ”因举声哭，门下惊，皆奔入满侧。

translations.literal: Thereupon he raised his voice and wept; gate retainers were startled and all ran in filling his sides.
translations.idiomatic: He burst into a wail; the porters panicked and crowded the room.

sentences.zh: 陟知其非常人，乃起，延与语，大奇之。

translations.literal: Zhi knew he was no ordinary man, rose, extended talk with him, marveled at him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Yang saw he was no commoner, rose, and talked until he marveled.

sentences.zh: 谓曰：“子出矣。

translations.literal: He said to him: "You may go."
translations.idiomatic: He told him, "You may go now."

sentences.zh: ”陟明旦大从车骑，奉谒造壹。

translations.literal: " Zhi the next morning with great train of vehicles and horsemen came paying formal visit to Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Next morning Yang arrived in full escort to return the call.

sentences.zh: 时，诸计吏多盛饬车马帷幕，而壹独柴车草屏，露宿其傍，延陟前坐于车下，左右莫不叹愕。

translations.literal: At the time many clerks had lavishly decked carriages and curtains; Yi alone had a brushwood cart and grass screen, lodged in the open beside it, extended Zhi to sit before him under the cart—left and right none did not sigh in awe.
translations.idiomatic: Other clerks rode silken curtains and fine teams; Zhao Yi slept in the dust beside a brush cart and bade Yang sit with him in the road—every onlooker gaped.

sentences.zh: 陟遂与言谈，至熏夕，极欢而去，执其手曰：“良璞不剖，必有泣血以相明者矣！

translations.literal: Zhi thereupon conversed with him until twilight smoke, utmost joy then parted, grasped his hand: "Fine jade uncut—there must be one weeping blood to make it plain!"
translations.idiomatic: They talked from noon till dusk in perfect joy; Yang clasped his hand: "Uncut jade weeps blood until a true judge sees it!"

sentences.zh: ”陟乃与袁逢共称荐之。

translations.literal: " Zhi then with Yuan Feng jointly praised and recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhi and Yuan Feng then jointly recommended him.

sentences.zh: 名动京师，士大夫想望其风采。

translations.literal: His name shook the capital; gentlemen cherished his bearing.
translations.idiomatic: His name thundered through Luoyang; every scholar dreamed of meeting him.

sentences.zh: 及西还，道经弘农，过侯太守皇甫规，门者不即通，壹遂遁去。

translations.literal: Returning west he passed through Hongnong, visited Grand Warden Marquis Huangfu Gui; the gatekeeper did not admit at once, Yi then slipped away.
translations.idiomatic: On the road west he stopped at Hongnong to see Grand Warden Huangfu Gui; the porter stalled him, and Zhao Yi vanished.

sentences.zh: 门吏惧，以白之，规闻壹名大惊，乃追书谢曰：“蹉跌不面，企德怀风，虚心委质，为日久矣。

translations.literal: Gate clerks feared, reported to him; Gui heard Yi's name and was greatly startled, then sent a letter apologizing: "Stumbling missed meeting you; standing on tiptoe I cherish your virtue and wind—humble heart offered substance—for long."
translations.idiomatic: The terrified porter told his master; Huangfu, hearing it was Zhao Yi, sent a frantic apology: "A blunder kept us apart; I have long stood on tiptoe for your virtue and offered my heart—too long."

sentences.zh: 侧闻仁者愍其区区，冀承清诲，以释遥悚。

translations.literal: I have heard sidelong that the humane pity my petty self—I hope to receive clear instruction to dispel distant dread.
translations.idiomatic: I hear the humane pity my trifling self—I beg one clear word to ease my distant fear.

sentences.zh: 今旦，外白有一尉两计吏，不道屈尊门下，更启乃知已去。

translations.literal: This morning outside reported one commandant and two clerks—I failed to have them condescend to my gate—opening again I learned they had already gone.
translations.idiomatic: This dawn my man said a captain and two clerks had come; I failed to welcome them at the gate—when I opened the message they were gone.

sentences.zh: 如印绶可投，夜岂待旦。

translations.literal: If the seal-ribbon may be cast off, why wait the night till dawn?
translations.idiomatic: Had I known, I would have flung away my seal that very night—why wait for morning?

sentences.zh: 惟君明睿，平其夙心。

translations.literal: Only you, clear-sighted, may calm your long-standing mind.
translations.idiomatic: Only your clear mind can quiet the heart I have long nursed.

sentences.zh: 宁当慢慠，加于所天。

translations.literal: How should sluggish pride be added to one's Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Surely you will not heap cold pride on the man you call lord of life?

sentences.zh: 事在悖惑，不足具责。

translations.literal: The affair lay in muddle and confusion—not worth detailing blame.
translations.idiomatic: The fault was blind confusion—not worth a full reckoning of blame.

sentences.zh: 倘可原察，追修前好，则何福如之！

translations.literal: If you might investigate and forgive, renew former good—then what fortune could match it!"
translations.idiomatic: If you can forgive and renew our old bond, what blessing could match that?"

sentences.zh: 谨遣主簿奉书。

translations.literal: Respectfully I send the chief clerk to present this letter.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully dispatch my chief clerk to deliver this letter.

sentences.zh: 下笔气结，汗流竟趾。

translations.literal: Putting brush to paper my breath knots; sweat streams to my toes.
translations.idiomatic: As I set brush to silk my chest tightens and sweat runs to my feet.

sentences.zh: ”壹报曰：“君学成师范，缙绅归慕，仰高希骥，历年滋多。

translations.literal: " Yi replied: "You, sir, have completed learning and are model for teachers; girdled-sash gentlemen turn to you in admiration; looking up high they hope to match your team—year on year it grows.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yi answered: "You have finished your studies and become a teacher to others; the gentry flock to you; they have long gazed up hoping to run in your traces.

sentences.zh: 旋辕兼道，渴于言侍，沐浴晨兴，昧旦守门，实望仁君，昭其悬迟。

translations.literal: Turning the carriage double distance, I thirsted for speech in attendance; bathing, I rose at dawn, before dawn kept the gate—truly I hoped a humane lord would lighten my long suspense.
translations.idiomatic: I doubled the road to reach you, hungering for conversation; I bathed, rose before light, and waited at your gate—truly I hoped a humane lord would end my long vigil.

sentences.zh: 以贵下贱，握发垂接。

translations.literal: To condescend from nobility to the base, grasping hair half-washed to receive.
translations.idiomatic: You might stoop from high rank to low, interrupt even your toilet to welcome a caller.

sentences.zh: 高可敷玩坟典，起发圣意；

translations.literal: On high one might unfold and play with tomb classics, rousing the sage's intent;
translations.idiomatic: On the lofty plane you might unfold the canon and stir a sage's purpose;

sentences.zh: 下则抗论当世，消弭时灾。

translations.literal: below then debate hard issues of the age and dissolve the hour's disasters.
translations.idiomatic: on the practical plane debate the troubles of the day and lift present woes.

sentences.zh: 岂悟君子，自生怠倦，失恂恂善诱之德，同亡国骄惰之志！

translations.literal: How could I have thought a gentleman would himself grow slack and weary, lose the virtue of kindly, step-by-step guidance, and share the proud sloth of a ruined state!"
translations.idiomatic: Never did I think a gentleman would grow indolent, abandon the gentle art of leading others, and sink to the arrogance of a dying kingdom!"

sentences.zh: 盖见机而作，不俟终日，是以夙退自引，畏使君劳。

translations.literal: Therefore seeing the moment and acting, not waiting the whole day—therefore I withdrew early on my own, fearing to weary my lord.
translations.idiomatic: The wise move when they see the sign, not at sunset—so I slipped away early, lest I burden you further.

sentences.zh: 昔人或历说而不遇，或思士而无从，皆归之于天，不尤于物。

translations.literal: Men of old sometimes discoursed everywhere yet did not meet recognition; sometimes longed for a gentleman yet had no access—all attributed it to Heaven, not blamed things.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient worthies sometimes preached and found no patron, sometimes yearned for a lord and met closed doors—they blamed Heaven, not the world.

sentences.zh: 今壹自谴而已，岂敢有猜！

translations.literal: Now Yi only blames himself—how dare harbor suspicion!
translations.idiomatic: I blame only myself—how should I suspect you?

sentences.zh: 仁君忽一匹夫，于德何损？

translations.literal: If a humane lord overlooks one commoner—what harm to his virtue?
translations.idiomatic: For a humane lord to overlook one nobody—what stain is that on his virtue?

sentences.zh: 而远辱手笔，追路相寻，诚足愧也。

translations.literal: Yet from afar you humiliated your brush, chased the road seeking me—truly enough to make me ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you troubled your brush and sent men down the road after me—enough to humble me.

sentences.zh: 壹之区区，曷云量己？

translations.literal: Yi's petty self—how can it speak of measuring itself?
translations.idiomatic: What trifle am I to speak of knowing my measure?

sentences.zh: 其嗟可去，谢也可食，诚则顽薄，实识其趣。

translations.literal: When the scolding may go, the apology may be eaten—though indeed stubborn and shallow, I truly grasp the point.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebuke may be withdrawn, the apology may be accepted—I am coarse, yet I understand the point of the Analects.

sentences.zh: 但关节□动，膝炙坏溃，请俟他日，乃奉其情。

translations.literal: Only my joints ache and shift, moxa burns have festered—please wait another day, then I will offer my feelings.
translations.idiomatic: My joints trouble me and old moxa sores weep—ask me another day and I will lay out my heart.

sentences.zh: 辄诵来贶，永以自慰。

translations.literal: For now I chant your gift and ever take comfort in it.
translations.idiomatic: For now I treasure your letter and draw comfort from it.

sentences.zh: ”遂去不顾。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he left and did not look back.
translations.idiomatic: With that he walked away and never looked back.

sentences.zh: 州郡争致礼命，十辟公府，并不就，终于家。

translations.literal: Commanderies and prefectures vied to extend ritual summons; ten times he was summoned to the excellencies' offices—none did he accept; he ended at home.
translations.idiomatic: Provinces competed to honor him; the high ministries called him ten times—he never went, and died at home.

sentences.zh: 初袁逢使善相者相壹，云“仕不过郡吏”，竟如其言。

translations.literal: Earlier Yuan Feng had a skilled physiognomist read Yi, who said "Office will not pass commandery clerk"—in the end it was as he said.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yuan Feng had a face-reader study Zhao Yi, who predicted he would never rise above a commandery clerk—it proved true.

sentences.zh: 著赋、颂、箴、诔、书、论及杂文十六篇。

translations.literal: He authored fu, odes, admonitions, dirges, letters, disquisitions, and miscellaneous pieces—sixteen in all.
translations.idiomatic: His rhapsodies, hymns, admonitions, laments, letters, essays, and miscellanea number sixteen.

sentences.zh: 刘梁字曼山，一名岑，东平宁阳人也。

translations.literal: Liu Liang, courtesy name Manshan, also called Cen, was a man of Ningyang in Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Liang, courtesy name Manshan, also known as Cen, came from Ningyang in Dongping.

sentences.zh: 梁宗室子孙，而少孤贫，卖书于市以自资。

translations.literal: Liang was a descendant of the royal house yet in youth was orphaned and poor, selling books in the market to support himself.
translations.idiomatic: A cadet of the Han imperial clan, he was orphaned and poor as a boy and peddled books in the market to live.

sentences.zh: 常疾世多利交，以邪曲相党，乃著《破群论》。

translations.literal: He constantly hated that the age had many profit-driven associations, that men factioned by crooked ways; therefore he composed "Smashing Factions."
translations.idiomatic: He loathed an age of mercenary cliques and crooked cabals, and wrote "Breaking the Clique."

sentences.zh: 时之览者以为：“仲尼作《春秋》，乱臣知惧。

translations.literal: Readers of the time thought: "When Zhongni made the Spring and Autumn, traitorous ministers knew fear.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporary readers said: "Confucius wrote the Spring and Autumn and wicked ministers trembled.

sentences.zh: 今此论之作，俗士岂不愧心！

translations.literal: Now with this treatise's composition, can vulgar scholars not feel shame in their hearts!"
translations.idiomatic: With this essay abroad, can shallow men not blush?"

sentences.zh: ”其文不存。

translations.literal: " Its text does not survive.
translations.idiomatic: The text itself is lost.

sentences.zh: 又著《辩和同之论》。

translations.literal: He also composed "Disquisition on Distinguishing Harmony from Sameness."
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote the "Disquisition on Harmony versus Conformity."

sentences.zh: 其辞曰：

translations.literal: Its wording says:
translations.idiomatic: It begins:

sentences.zh: 夫事有违而得道，有顺而失义，有爱而为害，有恶而为美。

translations.literal: Now affairs may oppose yet obtain the Way, comply yet lose right; there may be love that does harm, hate that does good.
translations.idiomatic: Some deeds run against the grain yet hit the Way; some follow custom yet miss justice; some kindness harms, some hatred heals.

sentences.zh: 其故何乎？

translations.literal: What is the reason?
translations.idiomatic: Why is that?

sentences.zh: 盖明智之所得，暗伪之所失也。

translations.literal: In general what the clear-sighted gain is what the dark and false lose.
translations.idiomatic: Because the clear-sighted seize what the deluded forfeit.

sentences.zh: 是以君子之于事也，无适无莫，必考之以义焉。

translations.literal: Therefore the gentleman's relation to affairs has no "this alone" or "that alone"—he must examine them with rightness.
translations.idiomatic: So the gentleman never says "only this" or "only that"—he tests every case by right.

sentences.zh: 得由和兴，失由同起，故以可济否谓之和，好恶不殊谓之同。

translations.literal: Gain arises from harmony, loss arises from sameness; therefore what can aid the blocked is called harmony, liking and hating undistinguished is called sameness.
translations.idiomatic: Success comes from harmony, ruin from blind sameness: harmony blends sour and bitter to save a dish; sameness is water poured on water.

sentences.zh: 《春秋传》曰：“和如羹焉，酸苦以剂其味，君子食之以平其心。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: "Harmony is like a stew—sour and bitter adjust the flavor; the gentleman eats it to calm his heart.
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo tradition says: "Harmony is like soup—sour and bitter balance the taste; the gentleman eats it to steady his mind.

sentences.zh: 同如水焉，若以水济水，谁能食之？

translations.literal: Sameness is like water—if with water you rescue water, who can eat it?
translations.idiomatic: Sameness is like plain water—who can drink water thickened with water?

sentences.zh: 琴瑟之专一，谁能听之？

translations.literal: Zither and se with one note only—who can listen?"
translations.idiomatic: If lute and zither play one note forever, who can bear to listen?"

sentences.zh: ”是以君子之行，周而不比，和而不同；

translations.literal: " Therefore the gentleman's conduct is comprehensive yet not partisan, harmonious yet not identical;
translations.idiomatic: Hence the gentleman is all-embracing without cabal, harmonious without mere conformity;

sentences.zh: 以救过为正，以匡恶为忠。

translations.literal: to set right error is correctness, to rescue evil is loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: to right a fault is uprightness, to cure vice is loyalty.

sentences.zh: 经曰：“将顺其美，匡救其恶，则上下和睦能相亲也。

translations.literal: The classic says: "Assist what is beautiful in him, rescue what is evil—then high and low are concordant and can draw near one another."
translations.idiomatic: The canon says: "Second the good in a ruler, mend the bad—then court and country meet in trust."

sentences.zh: 昔楚恭王有疾，召其大夫曰：“不谷不德，少主社稷。

translations.literal: Formerly King Gong of Chu was ill and summoned his great officers, saying: "I am not virtuous, in youth I took charge of the altars.
translations.idiomatic: King Gong of Chu fell ill and told his ministers: "I lack virtue; young, I took the throne.

sentences.zh: 失先君之绪，覆楚国之师，不谷之罪也。

translations.literal: I lost my former lord's continuity, overturned Chu's armies—it is my crime.
translations.idiomatic: I broke my father's line and shattered Chu's hosts—the fault is mine.

sentences.zh: 若以宗庙之灵，得保首领以殁，请为灵若厉。

translations.literal: If by the spirits of the ancestral temple I may keep my head to die, please give me the posthumous title Ling or Li."
translations.idiomatic: If the ancestors let me die with my head on my shoulders, bury me as "Ling" or "Li."

sentences.zh: ”大夫许诸。

translations.literal: " The great officers assented.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers agreed.

sentences.zh: 及其卒也，子囊曰：“不然。

translations.literal: When he died, Zinang said: "It is not so.
translations.idiomatic: At his death Zinang said: "Not so.

sentences.zh: 夫事君者，从其善，不从其过。

translations.literal: He who serves a lord follows his good, not his faults.
translations.idiomatic: A servant follows his lord's virtue, not his errors.

sentences.zh: 赫赫楚国，而君临之，抚正南海，训及诸夏，其宠大矣。

translations.literal: Brilliant is Chu, and you lorded over it, settled the south seas, instructed the central states—its favor was great.
translations.idiomatic: Mighty Chu lay in his hand; he steadied the southern sea and taught the central plain—his glory was vast.

sentences.zh: 有是宠也，而知其过，可不谓恭乎！

translations.literal: Having such favor yet knowing his faults—can this not be called Gong!"
translations.idiomatic: To hold such power yet know his own wrong—surely that is true reverence!"

sentences.zh: ”大夫众之。

translations.literal: " The great officers approved him.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers accepted this.

sentences.zh: 此讳而得道者也。

translations.literal: This is concealing fault yet obtaining the Way.
translations.idiomatic: That is hiding a ruler's shame yet serving the Way.

sentences.zh: 及灵王骄淫，暴虐无度，芋尹申亥从王之欲，以殡于乾溪，殉之二女。

translations.literal: When King Ling grew arrogant and dissolute, cruel without measure, the yu-yin Shen Hai followed the king's desires, buried him at Qianxi, and sacrificed two girls with him.
translations.idiomatic: King Ling turned wanton and savage; Shen Hai indulged his whims, laid him out at Qianxi, and buried two concubines alive at his side.

sentences.zh: 此顺而失义者也。

translations.literal: This is complying yet losing right.
translations.idiomatic: That is obeying a lord into injustice.

sentences.zh: 鄢陵之役，晋楚对战，阳穀献酒，子反以毙。

translations.literal: At the battle of Yanling, Jin and Chu faced each other; a man of Yanggu offered wine and Zifan died for it.
translations.idiomatic: At Yanling, when Jin met Chu, a native of Yanggu pressed wine on chief minister Zifan, who drank himself to death.

sentences.zh: 此爱而害之者也。

translations.literal: This is love that harmed him.
translations.idiomatic: That is fondness that killed him.

sentences.zh: 臧武仲曰：“孟孙之恶我，药石也；

translations.literal: Zang Wuzhong said: "Mengsun's hating me is medicine and stone;
translations.idiomatic: Zang Wuzhong said: "Mengsun's hatred is bitter physic;

sentences.zh: 季孙之爱我，美疢也。

translations.literal: Jisun's loving me is a lovely ulcer."
translations.idiomatic: Jisun's love is a pretty ulcer."

sentences.zh: 疢毒滋厚，石犹生我。

translations.literal: Ulcer poison grows thick—yet stone still gives me life.
translations.idiomatic: The sore may fester—yet the stone still saves my life.

sentences.zh: ”此恶而为美者也。

translations.literal: " This is hate that became good.
translations.idiomatic: That is harshness turned to blessing.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：“智之难也！

translations.literal: Confucius said: "How hard is wisdom!
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said: "How rare is true wisdom!

sentences.zh: 有臧武仲之智，而不容于鲁国，抑有由也。

translations.literal: Having Zang Wuzhong's wisdom, yet not tolerated in Lu—surely there was a reason.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Wuzhong was wise yet could not stay in Lu—there was cause.

sentences.zh: 作不顺而施不恕也。

translations.literal: His deeds were not compliant and his favors were not forgiving.
translations.idiomatic: His acts defied custom and his kindness lacked measure.

sentences.zh: ”盖善其知义，讥其违道也。

translations.literal: " In general he praised his knowing right and ridiculed his opposing the Way.
translations.idiomatic: So the sage praised his sense of justice and faulted his breach of the Way.

sentences.zh: 夫知而违之，伪也；

translations.literal: To know yet oppose it is falsity;
translations.idiomatic: To know the right and flout it is hypocrisy;

sentences.zh: 不知而失之，暗也。

translations.literal: not to know and miss it is darkness.
translations.idiomatic: not to know and miss it is folly.

sentences.zh: 暗为伪焉，其患一也。

translations.literal: Darkness becomes falsity—the mischief is one.
translations.idiomatic: Folly and hypocrisy breed the same harm.

sentences.zh: 患之所在，非徒在智之不及，又在及而违这者矣。

translations.literal: Where the mischief lies is not only in wisdom's failing to reach; it is also in reaching yet opposing.
translations.idiomatic: The danger lies not only in short wit but in having wit and turning it against the good.

sentences.zh: 故曰“智及之，仁不能守之，虽得之，必失之”也。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: "If wisdom reaches it but benevolence cannot guard it, though obtained, it will certainly be lost."
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying: "Insight without humanity cannot keep a gain—it slips away."

sentences.zh: 《夏书》曰：“念兹在兹，庶事恕施。

translations.literal: The Documents of Xia say: "Think of this here, think of this there; in many tasks apply forgiving kindness."
translations.idiomatic: The Xia Documents say: "Keep the charge in mind; in every task be generous."

sentences.zh: ”忠智之谓矣。

translations.literal: " This speaks of loyal wisdom.
translations.idiomatic: That is loyal wisdom.

sentences.zh: 故君子之行，动则思义，不为利回，不为义疚，进退周旋，唯道是务。

translations.literal: Therefore the gentleman's conduct, when he moves, thinks of rightness; he does not twist for profit, does not ache for partiality; advancing, withdrawing, turning, all—only the Way is his business.
translations.idiomatic: So the gentleman weighs every step by duty—never swerves for gain nor bends for favor; come or go, he serves only the Way.

sentences.zh: 苟失其道，则兄弟不阿；

translations.literal: If he loses the Way, then brothers do not indulge;
translations.idiomatic: Miss the Way and even brothers will not humor you;

sentences.zh: 苟得其义，虽仇雠不废。

translations.literal: If he obtains rightness, even enemies are not cast aside.
translations.idiomatic: Hit the mark and even foes may stand by you.

sentences.zh: 故解狐蒙祁奚之荐，二叔被周公之害，勃鞮以逆文为成，傅瑕以顺厉为败，管苏以憎忤取进，申侯以爱从见退：考之以义也。

translations.literal: Therefore Xie Hu received Qi Xi's recommendation though obscure; the two uncles suffered Zhou Gong's punishment; Bo Di made defying Duke Wen into success; Fu Xia made obeying Prince Li into ruin; Guan Su advanced through hated bluntness; Shen Hou was dismissed through compliant favor: all examined by rightness.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Xie Hu won Qi Xi's nomination from obscurity; Guan and Cai felt the Duke of Zhou's weight; Bo Di's defiance of Duke Wen proved loyal; Fu Xia's obedience to Prince Li brought ruin; Guan Su rose by blunt honesty; Shen Hou fell by flattery—all judged by right.

sentences.zh: 故曰：“不在逆顺，以义为断；

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: "It lies not in opposition or compliance—use rightness as the measure;
translations.idiomatic: So the maxim runs: "Judge not by yes or no but by justice;

sentences.zh: 不在憎爱，以道为贵。

translations.literal: it lies not in hate or love—honor the Way as precious."
translations.idiomatic: weigh not love or hate but hold the Way dear."

sentences.zh: ”《礼记》曰：“爱而知其恶，憎而知其善。

translations.literal: " The Record of Rites says: "Love him yet know his evil; hate him yet know his good."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Rites says: "Love a man yet mark his faults; hate him yet admit his virtues."

sentences.zh: ”考义之谓也。

translations.literal: " This speaks of examining rightness.
translations.idiomatic: That is judging by right.

sentences.zh: 桓帝时，举孝廉，除北新城长。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Huan he was raised filial and incorrupt, removed as magistrate of northern Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Huan he was nominated filial and incorrupt and made magistrate of northern Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 告县人曰：“昔文翁在蜀，道著巴汉；

translations.literal: He announced to the county people: "Long ago Wen Weng was in Shu—the Way shone through Ba and Han;
translations.idiomatic: He told his people: "Wen Weng in Shu spread the Way from Ba to Han;

sentences.zh: 庚桑琐隶，风移碨磥。

translations.literal: Gengsang Chu, a petty clerk, shifted the wind of stony custom.
translations.idiomatic: Gengsang Chu, a humble scribe, moved the hardest hill folk.

sentences.zh: 吾虽小宰，犹有社稷，苟赴期会，理文墨，岂本志乎！

translations.literal: I am though a small magistrate, still there are altars of soil and grain—if I merely rush to meetings and shuffle ink, is that my original intent!"
translations.idiomatic: I am only a petty magistrate, yet I hold the town's earth-god—shall I do nothing but chase deadlines and shuffle papers?"

sentences.zh: ”乃更大作讲舍，延聚生徙数百人，朝夕自往劝诫，身执经卷，试策殿最，儒化大行。

translations.literal: " Thereupon on a large scale he built lecture halls, gathered several hundred students, morning and evening personally went to exhort them, personally held the classics scrolls, examined them by questions and ranked best and worst—Confucian transformation greatly flourished.
translations.idiomatic: He then built great lecture halls, drew hundreds of scholars, taught morning and night, held the classics in his own hands, examined them by essay and rank—until Confucian learning flooded the district.

sentences.zh: 此邑至后犹称其教焉。

translations.literal: This district even afterward still praised his instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Long after, the county still praised his teaching.

sentences.zh: 特召入拜尚书郎。

translations.literal: He was specially summoned, entered, and was appointed gentleman of the masters of writing.
translations.idiomatic: The court specially summoned him and named him gentleman of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 累迁，后为野王令，未行。

translations.literal: By cumulative promotion he later became magistrate of Yewang; he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to magistrate of Yewang but never took up the post.

sentences.zh: 光和中，病卒。

translations.literal: In the Guanghe era he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness during Guanghe.

sentences.zh: 孙桢，亦以文才知名。

translations.literal: Sun Zhen also was known for literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zhen likewise won fame as a writer.

sentences.zh: 边让字文礼，除留浚仪人也。

translations.literal: Bian Rang, courtesy name Wenli, was a man of Junyi in Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Rang, courtesy name Wenli, came from Junyi in Chenliu commandery.

sentences.zh: 少辩博，能属文。

translations.literal: In youth he was disputatious and broadly learned, able to compose linked writing.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was eloquent, well read, and skilled at composition.

sentences.zh: 作《章华赋》，虽多淫丽之辞，而终之以正，亦如相如之讽也。

translations.literal: He composed the "Rhapsody on Zhanghua"; though it has many sensual and ornate phrases, in the end it concludes with rectitude—like Xiangru's indirect remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Zhanghua Rhapsody: though lush and sensual, it ends in moral correction—like Sima Xiangru's veiled counsel.

sentences.zh: 其辞曰：

translations.literal: Its wording says:
translations.idiomatic: It opens:

sentences.zh: 楚灵王既游云梦之泽，息于荆台之上。

translations.literal: King Ling of Chu had toured the marsh of Cloud Dream and rested on the terrace of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: King Ling of Chu had roamed Cloud Dream marsh and halted on Jing Terrace.

sentences.zh: 前方淮之水，左洞庭之波，右顾彭蠡之□，南眺巫山之阿。

translations.literal: Ahead lay the Huai's waters, to the left the waves of Dongting, to the right he gazed on Pengli's depths, southward he peered toward the slopes of Mount Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Before him ran the Huai, on his left rolled Dongting, on his right spread Pengli, to the south rose the shoulders of Wu Mountain.

sentences.zh: 延目广望，聘观终日。

translations.literal: He stretched his eyes in wide gaze and galloped his sight a whole day.
translations.idiomatic: He let his gaze roam and feasted his eyes from dawn to dusk.

sentences.zh: 顾谓左史倚相曰：“盛哉斯乐，可以遗老而忘死也！

translations.literal: Looking back he said to the left scribe Yi Xiang: "How grand this joy—it can send off old age and make one forget death!"
translations.idiomatic: He turned to his chronicler Yi Xiang and cried: "What bliss—enough to age a man in peace and make him forget death!"

sentences.zh: ”于是遂作章华之台，筑乾谿之室，穷木土之技，单珍府之实。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he built the terrace of Zhanghua, raised chambers at Qianxi, exhausted the craft of wood and earth, emptied the treasury's treasures.
translations.idiomatic: He then raised Zhanghua Tower, built halls at Qianxi, wrung the last trick from carpenters and masons, and drained the vaults of every gem.

sentences.zh: 举国营之，数年乃成。

translations.literal: The whole state labored at it; only after several years was it finished.
translations.idiomatic: The whole kingdom toiled for years before it stood.

sentences.zh: 设长夜之淫宴，作北里之新声。

translations.literal: He set night-long debauched feasts and made new songs of the northern lane.
translations.idiomatic: He staged all-night orgies and staged the licentious music of the northern quarter.

sentences.zh: 于是伍举知夫陈、蔡之将生谋也。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wu Ju knew that Chen and Cai would soon breed plots.
translations.idiomatic: Then Wu Ju saw that Chen and Cai would soon rise in treachery.

sentences.zh: 乃作斯赋以讽之：

translations.literal: Thereupon he composed this fu to admonish him:
translations.idiomatic: He therefore wrote this rhapsody to warn the king:

sentences.zh: 胄高阳之苗胤兮，承圣祖之洪泽。

translations.literal: Helm of Gaoyang's seedling-line; inheriting the vast grace of the sacred ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: He bears the blood of lofty Zhuanxu, the flood of merit from his royal forebears.

sentences.zh: 建列籓于南楚兮，等威灵于二伯。

translations.literal: He set feudal screens in southern Chu, matched awesome power with the two hegemons.
translations.idiomatic: He planted vassal walls in southern Chu and rivaled the twin hegemons in dread majesty.

sentences.zh: 超有商之大彭兮，越隆周之两虢。

translations.literal: He surpassed Shang's mighty Pengs, outran Zhou's paired Guo.
translations.idiomatic: He outshone Great Peng of Yin and strode past the two Guo of high Zhou.

sentences.zh: 达皇佐之高勋兮，驰仁声之显赫。

translations.literal: He reached the high merit of royal assistants, galloped the bright fame of humane renown.
translations.idiomatic: He touched the deeds of kingly ministers and rode the thunder of a humane name.

sentences.zh: 惠风春施，神武电断，华夏肃清，五服攸乱。

translations.literal: Kind wind spread like spring; divine martial judgment flashed like lightning; the Hua heartland was swept clean; the five zones knew order.
translations.idiomatic: Mercy blew soft as spring; his war-god wrath split like lightning; the central plain grew still; the five domains fell into rank.

sentences.zh: 旦垂精于万机兮，夕回辇于门馆。

translations.literal: Dawn he bent mind on myriad threads; dusk he wheeled his carriage back to gate and hall.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he weighed the myriad threads of state; at dusk he rolled his chariot home to palace gate.

sentences.zh: 设长夜之欢饮兮，展中情之□婉。

translations.literal: He set night-long revel feasts, unfolded inner hearts' tender grace.
translations.idiomatic: He staged feasts that ran till dawn and laid bare every tender whim.

sentences.zh: 竭四海之妙珍兮，尽生人之秘玩。

translations.literal: He drained the four seas' rare treasures, exhausted the living world's secret playthings.
translations.idiomatic: He emptied the four seas of wonders and the world of every hidden delight.

sentences.zh: 尔乃携窈窕，从好仇，径肉林，登糟丘，兰肴山竦，椒酒渊流。

translations.literal: Then he led slim beauties, followed lovely mates, crossed the Forest of Flesh, climbed the Hill of Lees—orchid viands piled like peaks, peppered wine flowed deep as a pool.
translations.idiomatic: He took slender beauties and fond companions through the "meat forest" and over the "dregs hill"—spiced meats stacked like mountains, pepper wine poured deep as a pool.

sentences.zh: 激玄醴于清池兮，靡微风而行舟。

translations.literal: He whipped dark sweet wine in clear pools, skimmed faint breeze to drive the boats.
translations.idiomatic: He lashed dark wine in clear pools and let a breath of wind rock the pleasure boats.

sentences.zh: 登瑶台以回望兮，冀弥日而消忧。

translations.literal: He mounted the jade terrace to look back, hoped a full day would melt his care.
translations.idiomatic: He climbed the jade belvedere to gaze abroad, hoping a whole sun would drown his sorrow.

sentences.zh: 于是招宓妃，命湘娥，齐倡列，郑女罗。

translations.literal: Then he summoned Fufei, commanded the Xiang goddesses, ranked Qi singers, spread Zheng maidens in a net.
translations.idiomatic: He called river goddesses, lined up Qi choruses, and netted Zheng's dancing girls.

sentences.zh: 扬《激楚》之清宫兮，展新声而长歌。

translations.literal: He raised the "Rushing Chu" in pure palace keys, stretched new tunes in long-drawn song.
translations.idiomatic: He raised the "Rushing Chu" in clear mode and spun fresh melodies in endless song.

sentences.zh: 繁手超于北里，妙舞丽于《阳阿》。

translations.literal: Busy fingers outdid the northern lane; subtle dance outshone "Yang'e."
translations.idiomatic: Dizzy fingerwork outdid the brothel lane; the dance eclipsed the famous "Yang'e."

sentences.zh: 金石类聚，丝竹群分。

translations.literal: Metal and stone clustered; silk and bamboo divided in choirs.
translations.idiomatic: Bronze and jade chimed together; strings and pipes answered in parts.

sentences.zh: 神轻袿，曳华文，罗衣飘颻，组绮缤纷。

translations.literal: Spirits shook light gowns, trailed patterned splendor—gauze robes fluttered, sash-silk flashed every hue.
translations.idiomatic: Girls shook thin sleeves and trailed brocade—silks streamed color on color.

sentences.zh: 纵轻躯以迅赴，若孤鹄之失群；

translations.literal: They flung lithe bodies in swift advance like lone swans dropped from the flock;
translations.idiomatic: They hurled slim forms like swans torn from the skein;

sentences.zh: 振华袂以逶迤，若游龙之登云。

translations.literal: they flourished bright sleeves in long curves like dragons climbing cloud.
translations.idiomatic: they flung bright sleeves like dragons mounting mist.

sentences.zh: 于是欢嬿既洽，长夜向半，琴瑟易调，繁手改弹。

translations.literal: Then joy had run its course, the long night neared half, zither and se changed tuning, busy fingers struck new strains.
translations.idiomatic: When delight peaked and midnight neared, lutes changed key and fingers raced new bars.

sentences.zh: 清声发而响激，微音逝而流散。

translations.literal: Clear tones burst sharp and ringing, faint notes died away in drifting scatter.
translations.idiomatic: Clear notes cracked like ice; soft phrases melted into air.

sentences.zh: 振弱支而纡绕兮，若绿繁之垂干；

translations.literal: They shook slender limbs in winding coils like green wisteria hanging from the bough;
translations.idiomatic: Arms wove like vine on the branch;

sentences.zh: 忽飘飖以轻逝兮，似鸾飞于天汉。

translations.literal: suddenly they floated off light as gone, like luan-birds in the Milky Way.
translations.idiomatic: then they floated away like luan flying the River of Stars.

sentences.zh: 舞无常态，鼓无定节，寻声响应，修短靡跌。

translations.literal: The dance kept no fixed shape, drums no fixed beat—they chased each sound, long and short never tripped.
translations.idiomatic: No step held still, no drum kept time—they followed every note, never missing a beat.

sentences.zh: 长袖奋而生风，清气激而绕结。

translations.literal: Long sleeves whipped a wind; pure breath surged and knotted round.
translations.idiomatic: Long sleeves raised a gale; clear air whirled and clung.

sentences.zh: 尔乃妍媚递进，巧弄相加，俯仰异容，忽兮神化。

translations.literal: Then loveliness mounted in turn, tricks piled one on another—now bent, now straight, faces shifted like spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Grace heaped on grace, each turn more cunning—bodies bent and flashed like shape-shifting ghosts.

sentences.zh: 体迅轻鸿，荣曜春华，进如浮云，退如激波。

translations.literal: Forms swift as light swans, glory bright as spring flowers—advancing like drifting cloud, withdrawing like a breaking wave.
translations.idiomatic: They moved light as swans, bright as spring blossom—forward like cloud, back like surf.

sentences.zh: 虽复柳惠，能不咨嗟！

translations.literal: Though you were Liu Xiahui, could you hold back a sigh!
translations.idiomatic: Even Liu Xiahui would have groaned at the sight!

sentences.zh: 于是天河既回，淫乐未终，清籥发徵，《激楚》扬风。

translations.literal: Then the River of Heaven had turned, debauch not yet ended—clear pipes sounded zhi, "Rushing Chu" rode the wind.
translations.idiomatic: The Dipper wheeled west, yet the orgy ran on—reed pipes shrilled zhi and "Rushing Chu" rode the gale.

sentences.zh: 于是音气发于丝竹兮，飞响轶于云中。

translations.literal: Then tone-breath rose from strings and pipes; flying echoes shot beyond the clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Music climbed from strings and pipes and pierced the clouds.

sentences.zh: 比目应节而双跃兮，孤雌感声而鸣雄。

translations.literal: Paired flatfish leapt to the beat; lone hen answered tone and called her mate.
translations.idiomatic: Twin fish jumped to the measure; a lone hen heard the tune and called her cock.

sentences.zh: 美繁手之轻妙兮，嘉新声之弥隆。

translations.literal: They praised the dancers' light skill, cheered the swelling new song.
translations.idiomatic: They praised the light-fingered art and the ever-richer air.

sentences.zh: 于是众变已尽，群乐既考。

translations.literal: Then every change was spent, all music had played its course.
translations.idiomatic: When every variation was done and every tune had sounded,

sentences.zh: 归乎生风之广夏兮，修黄轩之要道。

translations.literal: they returned to the wind-breeding great hall, walked the yellow chariot's royal way.
translations.idiomatic: they withdrew to the lofty hall where wind is born and trod the Yellow Emperor's road of rule.

sentences.zh: 携西子之弱腕兮，援毛嫔之素肘。

translations.literal: They took Xizi's fragile wrist, clasped Lady Mao's snowy elbow.
translations.idiomatic: They linked the wrist of Xishi, the arm of Lady Mao.

sentences.zh: 形便娟以婵媛兮，若流风之靡草。

translations.literal: Their shapes graceful and swaying like wind bending grass.
translations.idiomatic: Their bodies swayed soft as wind-stroked grass.

sentences.zh: 美仪操之姣丽兮，忽遗生而忘老。

translations.literal: Lovely bearing and carriage so fine they forgot life itself and old age.
translations.idiomatic: Such grace made them forget they lived and could grow old.

sentences.zh: 尔乃清夜晨，妙技单，收尊俎，彻鼓盘。

translations.literal: Then the clear night turned toward dawn, marvels were spent, wine vessels were gathered, drums and trays cleared away.
translations.idiomatic: When night thinned toward dawn the show ended—cups were cleared, drums stilled.

sentences.zh: 惘焉若酲，抚剑而叹。

translations.literal: Dazed as after wine, he stroked his sword and sighed.
translations.idiomatic: The king woke dazed as from wine, fingered his sword, and sighed.

sentences.zh: 虑理国之须才，悟稼穑之艰难。

translations.literal: He pondered that ordering the state needs talent, understood how bitter is the peasant's toil.
translations.idiomatic: He remembered that rule needs men of worth and that grain is bought with sweat.

sentences.zh: 美吕尚之佐周，善管仲之辅桓。

translations.literal: He praised Lü Shang's aid to Zhou, approved Guan Zhong's help to Huan.
translations.idiomatic: He praised Lü Wang's service to Zhou and Guan Zhong's work for Duke Huan.

sentences.zh: 将超世而作理，焉沈湎于此欢！

translations.literal: He would transcend the age to set the pattern—how could he drown in such delight!
translations.idiomatic: He would rise above the moment to govern—how stay sunk in pleasure?

sentences.zh: 于是罢女乐，堕瑶台。

translations.literal: Thereupon he dismissed the palace girls, toppled the jade terrace.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the dancers away and pulled down the jade tower.

sentences.zh: 思夏禹之卑官，慕有虞之土阶。

translations.literal: He thought of Yu's low halls, envied Shun's earthen steps.
translations.idiomatic: He recalled Yu's plain halls and envied Shun's mud steps.

sentences.zh: 举英奇于仄陋，拔髦秀于蓬莱。

translations.literal: He raised the strange and splendid from mean alleys, plucked finest shoots from Penglai.
translations.idiomatic: He lifted genius from the lanes and plucked excellence as from fairy isle.

sentences.zh: 君明哲以知人，官随任而处能。

translations.literal: The lord was clear-sighted in knowing men; offices matched talents wherever placed.
translations.idiomatic: The king read men clearly and set every post to its gift.

sentences.zh: 百揆时叙，庶绩咸熙。

translations.literal: All bureaus kept their seasons; every task shone with success.
translations.idiomatic: Every ministry ran in season; every deed shone bright.

sentences.zh: 诸侯慕义，不召同期。

translations.literal: Feudal lords admired his rightness, came without summons at the same hour.
translations.idiomatic: Lords loved his justice and gathered without call.

sentences.zh: 继高阳之绝轨，崇成、庄之洪基。

translations.literal: He continued Gaoyang's broken track, raised Cheng and Zhuang's mighty base.
translations.idiomatic: He mended Zhuanxu's broken line and widened Cheng and Zhuang's foundation.

sentences.zh: 虽齐醒之一匡，岂足方于大持？

translations.literal: Though Qi's single sobering saved the realm—how can that match this great grip!
translations.idiomatic: Even the one great sobering of Qi cannot equal this grasp of power!

sentences.zh: 尔乃育之以仁，临之以明。

translations.literal: Then he nurtured them with kindness, faced them with clarity.
translations.idiomatic: He fed the people with mercy and met them with clear sight.

sentences.zh: 致虔报于鬼神，尽肃恭乎上京。

translations.literal: He showed reverent thanks to ghosts and gods, kept full respect toward high capital.
translations.idiomatic: He thanked heaven and earth with awe and bowed toward the royal seat.

sentences.zh: 驰淳化于黎元，永历世而太平。

translations.literal: He drove pure teaching into the black-haired folk, stretched peace through endless reigns.
translations.idiomatic: He poured honest rule through the people and promised ages of calm.

sentences.zh: 大将军何进闻让才名，欲辟命之。

translations.literal: Grand General He Jin heard Rang's literary fame and wished to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: He Jin heard Bian Rang's name and wanted him on staff.

sentences.zh: 恐不至，诡以军事征召。

translations.literal: Fearing he would not come, he feigned a military summons.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing refusal, he tricked him with a martial call-up.

sentences.zh: 既到，署令史，进以礼见之。

translations.literal: When he arrived, he was appointed clerk; He Jin received him with full rites.
translations.idiomatic: When he came, He Jin named him clerk and greeted him with ceremony.

sentences.zh: 让善占射，能辞对。

translations.literal: Rang was skilled in riddling and repartee, able in debate.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Rang excelled at wit contests and sharp dialogue.

sentences.zh: 时，宾客满堂，莫不羡其风。

translations.literal: At the time guests filled the hall; none did not envy his manner.
translations.idiomatic: The hall was packed with guests, all envying his bearing.

sentences.zh: 府掾孔融、王朗并修刺候焉。

translations.literal: House clerks Kong Rong and Wang Lang both sent visiting cards to wait on him.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Rong and Wang Lang, aides in the bureau, both left cards to pay court.

sentences.zh: 议郎蔡邕深敬之，以为让宜处高任，乃荐于何进曰：

translations.literal: Gentleman Consultant Cai Yong deeply respected him, thought Rang fit for high duty, and therefore recommended to He Jin, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yong revered him, argued he deserved high office, and wrote He Jin:

sentences.zh: 伏惟幕府初开，博选清英，华发旧德，并为元鬼。

translations.literal: I prostrate myself: though your headquarters newly opens and broadly selects the pure and bright, the grey-haired elders of old virtue together form your tortoise-shell council—
translations.idiomatic: Your new staff picks the best, yet your hoary counselors already match the flock of herons at Yong or the host at Zhou's court—

sentences.zh: 虽振鹭之集西雍，济济之在周庭，无以或加。

translations.literal: though the herons gather at western Yong, the throng stands in Zhou's court—nothing could add to it.
translations.idiomatic: nothing could improve that array.

sentences.zh: 窃见令史陈留边让，天授逸才，聪明贤智。

translations.literal: Privately I have seen Clerk Bian Rang of Chenliu—Heaven gave him soaring talent, clear wit, and sage intelligence.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I note your clerk Bian Rang of Chenliu—Heaven gave him winged genius and a lucid mind.

sentences.zh: 髫□夙孤，不尽家训。

translations.literal: His topknot years knew orphaning; he did not exhaust family instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he missed full family teaching.

sentences.zh: 及就学庐，便受大典。

translations.literal: When he reached the study hall, at once he received the great canons.
translations.idiomatic: Once he entered school he seized the great classics.

sentences.zh: 初涉诸经，见本知义。

translations.literal: At first wading the various scriptures, he saw the root and knew the meaning.
translations.idiomatic: He touched every classic, saw root and sense at once.

sentences.zh: 授者不能对其问，章句不能逮其意。

translations.literal: Teachers could not answer his questions; glosses could not catch his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Masters could not meet his questions; chapter-and-verse notes could not pin his thought.

sentences.zh: 心通性达，口辩辞长。

translations.literal: His heart penetrated, nature reached; mouth eloquent, phrasing long.
translations.idiomatic: His mind pierced principle, his tongue ran long with eloquence.

sentences.zh: 非礼不动，非法不言。

translations.literal: What was not ritual he did not move; what was not law he did not speak.
translations.idiomatic: He moved only by rite and spoke only by rule.

sentences.zh: 若处狐疑之论，定嫌审之分，经典交至，捡括参合，众夫寂焉，莫之能夺也。

translations.literal: If placed in doubtful debate, fixing fine points of suspicion, when classics cross-checked and evidence compared, the crowd falls silent—none can overthrow him.
translations.idiomatic: Set him a hard case, weigh fine points, pile text on text—men fall silent; none can refute him.

sentences.zh: 使让生在唐、虞，则元、凯之次，运值仲尼，则颜、冉之亚，岂徒俗之凡偶近器而已者哉！

translations.literal: Had Rang been born under Tang or Yu, he would rank after Yuan and Kai; had fortune matched Confucius, he would stand next to Yan and Ran—how could he be a vulgar mediocrity near at hand!
translations.idiomatic: Born under Yao and Shun he would walk with the Eight Yuan; meet Confucius and he would pace Yan and Ran—no mere hack of the market!

sentences.zh: 阶级名位，亦宜超然。

translations.literal: As to rank and title, he should likewise stand apart.
translations.idiomatic: His rank, too, should tower above the common.

sentences.zh: 若复随辈而进，非所以章瑰伟之高价，昭知人之绝明也。

translations.literal: If again he follows the herd in promotion, that is not how to display rare jade's high price or show matchless judgment of men.
translations.idiomatic: To advance him like any clerk is no way to show rare jade or prove you know men.

sentences.zh: 传曰：“函牛之鼎以亨鸡，多汁则淡而不可食，少计则熬而不可熟。

translations.literal: The tradition says: "The cauldron that holds an ox is used to boil a chicken—too much juice and it is thin and inedible, too little fire and it chars yet will not cook."
translations.idiomatic: The proverb runs: "A cauldron built for an ox should not stew a chick—too much broth makes thin soup, too little fire chars the meat."

sentences.zh: ”此言大器之于小用，固有所不宜也。

translations.literal: " This speaks of how a great vessel in petty use is of course unsuitable.
translations.idiomatic: So a great tool ill used is always wrong.

sentences.zh: 邕窃□邑，怪此宝鼎未受牺牛大羹之和，久在煎熬脔割之间。

translations.literal: Yong privately marvels that this treasure cauldron has not tasted the harmony of ox sacrifice and grand stew, but long broils in petty slicing.
translations.idiomatic: I marvel that this treasure cauldron never held the king's great sacrifice yet simmers in kitchen scraps.

sentences.zh: 愿明将军回谋垂虑，裁加少纳，贡之机密，展之力用。

translations.literal: I hope the bright general will turn his plan, bend thought, trim and admit a little, present him to secret counsel, stretch his strength to use.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you reconsider, take him in, seat him in your inner council, and use his power.

sentences.zh: 若以年齿为嫌，则颜回不得贯德行之首，子奇终无理阿之功。

translations.literal: If you scruple at age, then Yan Hui could not have led the list of virtue, and Ziqi would never have won merit at A.
translations.idiomatic: If youth bars him, Yan Hui would not head the virtuous, nor Ziqi win glory at A.

sentences.zh: 苟堪其事，古今一也。

translations.literal: If he can bear the charge, past and present are one.
translations.idiomatic: If he can do the work, age is nothing new under heaven.

sentences.zh: 让后以高才擢进，屡迁，出为九江太守，不以为能也。

translations.literal: Later Rang by high talent was promoted in steps, transferred out as grand warden of Jiujiang—this was not thought adequate.
translations.idiomatic: Later Bian Rang rose by talent and became grand warden of Jiujiang—still beneath his gifts.

sentences.zh: 初平中，王室大乱，让去官还家。

translations.literal: In the Chuping years the royal house fell into great chaos; Rang left office and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In Chuping the court collapsed; Bian Rang resigned and went home.

sentences.zh: 恃才气，不屈曹操，多轻侮之言。

translations.literal: Relying on talent and spirit, he would not bow to Cao Cao and often spoke slighting words.
translations.idiomatic: He trusted his gifts, refused to bend to Cao Cao, and sneered at him often.

sentences.zh: 建安中，其乡人有构让于操，操告郡就杀之。

translations.literal: In the Jian'an years a fellow villager framed Rang before Cao; Cao informed the commandery and had him killed.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian'an a townsman slandered him to Cao Cao, who ordered the commandery to execute him.

sentences.zh: 文多遗失。

translations.literal: Much of his writing is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Most of his writings are lost.

sentences.zh: 郦炎字文胜，范阳人，郦食其之后也。

translations.literal: Li Yan, courtesy name Wensheng, was a man of Fanyang, a descendant of Li Yiji.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yan, courtesy name Wensheng, came from Fanyang and traced descent from Li Yiji.

sentences.zh: 炎有文才，解音律，言论给捷，多服其能理。

translations.literal: Yan had literary talent, understood pitch and mode, speech quick and winning—many admired his ability to reason.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote well, knew music, spoke with a nimble tongue, and men praised his clear mind.

sentences.zh: 灵帝时，州郡辟命，皆不就，有志气。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Ling, prefectures summoned him; none did he accept—he had high resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ling every province called him; he refused all, holding fast to his purpose.

sentences.zh: 作诗二篇曰：

translations.literal: He composed two poems, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He left two poems:

sentences.zh: 大道夷且长，窘路狭且促。

translations.literal: The great Way is level and long; the straitened road is narrow and short.
translations.idiomatic: The high road runs wide and long; the trapped path is tight and brief.

sentences.zh: 修冀无卑栖，远趾不步局。

translations.literal: Long wings find no low roost; far hooves will not pace a small yard.
translations.idiomatic: Great wings scorn low branches; thousand-li hooves spurn a tiny yard.

sentences.zh: 舒吾陵霄羽，奋此千里足。

translations.literal: Spread my pinions to storm the clouds, flex these thousand-li feet.
translations.idiomatic: Spread my wings for the storm, stretch these thousand-li legs.

sentences.zh: 超迈绝尘驱，倏忽谁能逐。

translations.literal: I race beyond the dust—who in a flash can pursue?
translations.idiomatic: I outrun the dust—who can catch such a burst?

sentences.zh: 贤愚岂常类，禀性在清浊。

translations.literal: Are worthy and fool fixed classes? Nature lies in clear or turbid stuff.
translations.idiomatic: Wit and dullness are not fixed—character is clear or muddy by birth.

sentences.zh: 富贵有人籍，贫贱无天录。

translations.literal: The rich have human registers; the poor lack Heaven's scroll.
translations.idiomatic: Fortune keeps a roster for the rich; the poor are struck from Heaven's book.

sentences.zh: 通塞苟由已，志士不相卜。

translations.literal: If blockage and passage rest in oneself, the resolute do not divine with others.
translations.idiomatic: If fate is in your own hands, a hero asks no oracle.

sentences.zh: 陈平敖里社，韩信钓河曲。

translations.literal: Chen Ping lorded his village altar; Han Xin angled the river bend.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ping cut capers at the village shrine; Han Xin fished the river curve.

sentences.zh: 终居天下宰，食此万钟禄。

translations.literal: In the end they stood as lords under Heaven and ate the myriad zhong of salary.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they ruled the realm and drew the fattest stipends.

sentences.zh: 德音流千载，功名重山岳。

translations.literal: Their virtue-sound flows a thousand years; merit-weight tops mountain peaks.
translations.idiomatic: Their names still echo; their deeds outweigh mountains.

sentences.zh: 灵芝生河洲，动摇因洪波。

translations.literal: The numinous mushroom grows on the river isle, swayed by great waves.
translations.idiomatic: The magic fungus sprouts on the shoal, tossed by the flood.

sentences.zh: 兰荣一何晚，严霜瘁其柯。

translations.literal: How late the orchid blooms—hard frost withers its stem.
translations.idiomatic: The orchid opens late—bitter frost shrivels its stem.

sentences.zh: 哀哉二芳草，不植太山阿。

translations.literal: Alas for those two fragrant plants—not planted on Mount Tai's slope.
translations.idiomatic: Alas—two sweet herbs never rooted on Taishan's height.

sentences.zh: 文质道所贵，遭时用有嘉。

translations.literal: Pattern and substance are what the Way esteems; meeting the age they win praise.
translations.idiomatic: Wen and zhi are the Way's treasure; meet the right hour and they shine.

sentences.zh: 绛、灌临衡宰，谓谊崇浮华。

translations.literal: Zhou Bo and Guan Ying faced the boy minister at the balance and called Jia Yi mere empty show.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Bo and Guan Ying weighed the young steward and called Jia Yi hollow flash.

sentences.zh: 贤才抑不用，远投荆南沙。

translations.literal: Worthy talent was repressed and unused, cast far to the southern sands of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Genius was shelved and hurled to Jing's southern waste.

sentences.zh: 抱玉乘龙骥，不逢乐与和。

translations.literal: Embracing jade, riding dragon steeds—yet never meeting Yue and He.
translations.idiomatic: He hugged his jade and rode swift horses—yet never found Boya to hear his song.

sentences.zh: 安得孔仲尼，为世陈四科。

translations.literal: How can we get Kong Zhongni to lay out the four classes for the age?
translations.idiomatic: Where is a Confucius to rank the four kinds of men for this world?

sentences.zh: 炎后风病慌忽。

translations.literal: Afterward Yan suffered wind illness with confusion and distraction.
translations.idiomatic: Later Li Yan was stricken with a wind disorder that clouded his mind.

sentences.zh: 性至孝，遭母忧，病甚发动。

translations.literal: His nature was supremely filial; meeting mourning for his mother, the illness broke out severely.
translations.idiomatic: He was utterly filial; when his mother died the fit struck hard.

sentences.zh: 妻始产而惊死，妻家讼之，收系狱。

translations.literal: His wife had just given birth and died of fright; her family sued him, and he was seized and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: His wife died in childbirth from shock; her kin brought suit and had him jailed.

sentences.zh: 炎病不能理对，嘉平六年，遂死狱中，时年二十八。

translations.literal: Yan, ill, could not answer at trial; in the sixth year of Jiaping he therefore died in prison, age twenty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Too sick to plead at trial, he died in jail in Jiaping 6 at twenty-eight.

sentences.zh: 尚书卢植为之诔赞，以昭其懿德。

translations.literal: Minister of the Masters of Writing Lu Zhi composed a dirge-praise for him to display his fine virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi of the masters of writing wrote a lament to publish his noble character.

sentences.zh: 侯瑾字子瑜，敦煌人也。

translations.literal: Hou Jin, courtesy name Ziyu, was a man of Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jin, courtesy name Ziyu, came from Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 少孤贫，依宗人居。

translations.literal: In youth orphaned and poor, he lodged dependent on a clansman.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor, he lived under a kinsman's roof.

sentences.zh: 性笃学，恒佣作为资，暮还辄燃柴以读书。

translations.literal: By nature he loved learning; constantly he hired out labor for funds, and returning at evening always lit brushwood to read by.
translations.idiomatic: He loved books, hired himself out by day, and burned faggots to read by night.

sentences.zh: 常以礼自牧，独处一房，如对严宾焉。

translations.literal: He always restrained himself with ritual, dwelt alone in one chamber as if facing stern guests.
translations.idiomatic: He kept ritual discipline, sat alone in one room as if hosting strict elders.

sentences.zh: 州郡累召，公车有道征，并称疾不到。

translations.literal: Commanderies repeatedly summoned him; the state coach summoned him as "possessing the Way"—all he declined illness and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Provinces called him; the court summoned him as a man of the Way—each time he pleaded illness.

sentences.zh: 作《矫世论》以讥切当时，而徙入山中，覃思著述。

translations.literal: He composed "Correcting the Age" to satirize the time, then moved into the mountains and pondered writing deeply.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote "Correcting the Age" to skewer his day, then withdrew to the hills to think and write.

sentences.zh: 以莫知于世，故作《应宾难》以自寄。

translations.literal: Because none in the world knew him, he therefore composed "Replying to the Guest's Difficulties" to lodge his mind.
translations.idiomatic: Unknown to the world, he penned "Answering the Guest's Objections" to speak his mind.

sentences.zh: 又案《汉记》撰中兴以后行事，为《皇德传》三十篇，行于世。

translations.literal: Again he consulted the Han Records and compiled deeds after the restoration into thirty sections of "Traditions of August Virtue," which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He drew on the Han Records to chronicle the restored Han in thirty chapters of August Virtue Traditions.

sentences.zh: 余所作杂文数十篇，多亡失。

translations.literal: Several tens of miscellaneous pieces I composed are mostly lost.
translations.idiomatic: Dozens of my own essays are largely lost.

sentences.zh: 河西人敬其才而不敢名之，皆称为侯君云。

translations.literal: The people west of the river revered his talent and dared not speak his name, all calling him Lord Hou.
translations.idiomatic: West of the river men honored his gift and simply called him Lord Hou.

sentences.zh: 高彪字义方，吴郡无锡人也。

translations.literal: Gao Biao, courtesy name Yifang, was a man of Wuxi in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Biao, courtesy name Yifang, was from Wuxi in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 家本单寒，至彪为诸生，游太学。
