translations.literal: The family had been humble; by Biao's time he was a student and roamed the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: His house was poor; he became a student and studied at the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 有雅才而讷于言。

translations.literal: He had refined talent but was slow of tongue.
translations.idiomatic: He had elegant gifts but spoke with difficulty.

sentences.zh: 尝从马融欲访大义，融疾，不获见，乃复剌遗融书曰：“承服风问，从来有年，故不待介者而谒大君子之门，冀一见龙光，以叙腹心之愿。

translations.literal: Once he followed Ma Rong wishing to inquire into great meanings; Rong was ill and he could not obtain audience; therefore he again sent a visiting slip leaving Rong a letter: "Having heard your wind and questionings many years, I therefore did not wait for an intermediary to visit the gate of the great gentleman, hoping once to see dragon radiance and pour out the wish of my inmost heart.
translations.idiomatic: He sought Ma Rong's teaching; Ma was ill and shut the door, so Gao slipped in a letter: "Long I have heard your fame and meant to call without a go-between, hoping once to catch your light and speak my heart.

sentences.zh: 不图遭疾，幽闭莫启。

translations.literal: I did not expect to meet illness, darkly closed and never opened.
translations.idiomatic: I did not think to find you sealed away by sickness.

sentences.zh: 昔周公旦父文兄武，九命作伯，以尹华夏，犹挥沐吐餐，垂接白屋，故周道以隆，天下归德。

translations.literal: Anciently the Duke of Zhou had father Wen and brother Wu, received nine commands and became elder to shepherd the Hua lands—yet he wrung his dripping hair and spat out his food, bowing to receive men from thatched roofs; therefore Zhou's way rose and the world turned to his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou, though son of King Wen and brother of King Wu, though raised to elder regent of All-under-Heaven, still snatched time from bath and meal to greet poor scholars—so Zhou flourished and the realm loved his virtue.

sentences.zh: 公今养疴傲士，故其宜也。

translations.literal: Sir, now you nurse illness and disdain scholars—perhaps that is fitting."
translations.idiomatic: Sir, you hide behind illness and scorn visitors—perhaps that suits you."

sentences.zh: ”融省书惭，追谢还之，彪逝而不顾。

translations.literal: " Rong read the letter, felt shame, chased after him to apologize and return him—Biao went away and did not look back.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Rong read it, blushed, sent apologies and begged him back—Gao Biao walked on without turning.

sentences.zh: 后郡举孝廉，试经第一。

translations.literal: Later the commandery raised him filial and incorrupt; in classics examination he ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery nominated him filial and incorrupt; he topped the classics test.

sentences.zh: 除郎中，校书东观。

translations.literal: He was appointed gentleman of the interior and collator at the Eastern View.
translations.idiomatic: He became gentleman of the interior and collating secretary at the Eastern Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 数奏赋、颂、奇文，因事讽谏，灵帝异之。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he presented fu, odes, and strange writings, using affairs for indirect remonstrance—Emperor Ling marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: He sent up rhapsodies and essays that remonstrated by indirection; Emperor Ling wondered at him.

sentences.zh: 时，京兆第五永为督军御史，使督幽州。

translations.literal: At the time the capital-area Diwu Yong was supervising army censor, sent to supervise Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Diwu Yong of Jingzhao was army censor, ordered to oversee Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 百官大会，祖饯于长乐观。

translations.literal: The hundred officials held a great assembly and performed the road-leaving rite at the Changleguan.
translations.idiomatic: The whole bureaucracy gathered to toast his farewell at Changleguan.

sentences.zh: 议郎葵邑等皆赋诗，彪乃独作箴曰：“文武将坠，乃俾俊臣。

translations.literal: Gentleman consultants Cai Yong and others all composed poems; Biao alone composed an admonition: "Civil and martial are about to fall—therefore Heaven sends a splendid minister.
translations.idiomatic: Counsel gentlemen like Cai Yong wrote verse; Gao Biao alone offered an admonition: "When wen and wu falter, Heaven sends a splendid minister.

sentences.zh: 整我皇纲，董此不虔。

translations.literal: Set straight our royal net, oversee this irreverence."
translations.idiomatic: Straighten the royal net and watch this insolence."

sentences.zh: 古之君子，即戎忘身。

translations.literal: The gentleman of old, taking up arms, forgot self.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient worthies, once under arms, forgot private life.

sentences.zh: 明其果毅，尚其桓桓。

translations.literal: Make plain his firm resolve, honor his martial awe."
translations.idiomatic: Show his steadfast nerve, praise his tiger bearing."

sentences.zh: 吕尚七十，气冠三军，诗人作歌，如鹰如鹯。

translations.literal: Lü Shang at seventy, his spirit topped three armies—the poets sang him hawk and kite.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Wang at seventy outfaced three hosts—the Odes liken him to hawk and kite.

sentences.zh: 天有太一，五将三门；

translations.literal: Heaven has Grand Unity, five generals, three gates;
translations.idiomatic: Heaven holds the Grand One, five hosts, three gates;

sentences.zh: 地有九变，丘陵山川；

translations.literal: earth has nine changes, hills, mounds, streams, mountains;
translations.idiomatic: earth nine transformations of terrain;

sentences.zh: 人有计策，六奇五间。

translations.literal: man has stratagems, the six marvels, the five gaps."
translations.idiomatic: man has plans—the six wonders, the five rifts."

sentences.zh: 总兹三事，谋则咨询。

translations.literal: Total these three matters—in planning then consult."
translations.idiomatic: Weigh these three—in counsel seek help."

sentences.zh: 无曰己能，务在求贤，淮阴之勇，广野是尊。

translations.literal: Do not say "I myself am able"—strive to seek worthies; Han Xin's courage—Guangye honored him."
translations.idiomatic: Never cry "I alone can"—seek wise men; remember Han Xin, whom Guangwu esteemed."

sentences.zh: 周公大圣，石碏纯臣，以威克爱，以义灭亲。

translations.literal: The Duke of Zhou was great sage; Shi Que was pure minister—by awe they mastered love, by right they destroyed kin."
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Gong was paragon sage; Shi Que pure minister—they curbed favor with awe, cut kin by duty."

sentences.zh: 勿谓时险，不正其身。

translations.literal: Do not call the times perilous and fail to correct your person."
translations.idiomatic: Do not blame the times and neglect your own conduct."

sentences.zh: 勿谓无人，莫识己真。

translations.literal: Do not say there are no men—none knows your true self."
translations.idiomatic: Do not say no men remain—none has seen your truth."

sentences.zh: 忘富遗贵，福禄乃存。

translations.literal: Forget wealth, cast off rank—then blessing and salary endure."
translations.idiomatic: Forget riches, spurn station—then fortune endures."

sentences.zh: 枉道依合，复无所观。

translations.literal: Twist the Way to curry favor—again there is nothing worth seeing."
translations.idiomatic: Bend principle to fit the crowd—and nothing worth watching remains."

sentences.zh: 先公高节，越可永遵。

translations.literal: Your forebears' lofty integrity—how far it may be forever followed."
translations.idiomatic: Your fathers' high honor—follow it forever."

sentences.zh: 佩藏斯戒，以厉终身。

translations.literal: Wear this warning at the belt, to brace a lifetime."
translations.idiomatic: Hang this admonition on your sash for life."

sentences.zh: ”邕等甚美其文，以为莫尚也。

translations.literal: " Yong and the others greatly praised his writing, thinking none could surpass it.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yong and the rest extolled his lines above all others.

sentences.zh: 后迁外黄令，帝敕同僚临送，祖于上东门，诏东观画彪像以劝学者。

translations.literal: Later he was promoted magistrate of Waihuang; the emperor ordered colleagues to attend his send-off, performed the road rite at the Upper East Gate, and edicted the Eastern View to paint Biao's portrait to encourage students.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted magistrate of Waihuang, he was escorted by peers from the Upper East Gate, and the court ordered his portrait hung at the Eastern Pavilion to rouse scholars.

sentences.zh: 彪到官，有德政，上书荐县人申徒蟠等。

translations.literal: When Biao reached his post he had virtuous government and submitted a memorial recommending his county's Shen Tu Pan and others.
translations.idiomatic: At post he governed well and recommended Shen Tu Pan and other locals.

sentences.zh: 病卒于官，文章多亡。

translations.literal: He died of illness in office; much of his writing is lost.
translations.idiomatic: He died in harness; many works are gone.

sentences.zh: 子岱，亦知名。

translations.literal: His son Dai was also known.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gao Dai likewise won a name.

sentences.zh: 张超字子并，河间鄚人也，留侯良之后也。

translations.literal: Zhang Chao, courtesy name Zibing, was a man of Mo in Hejian, a descendant of Marquis Liu Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chao, courtesy name Zibing, came from Mo in Hejian and traced descent from Marquis Zhang Liang.

sentences.zh: 有文才。

translations.literal: He had literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote well.

sentences.zh: 灵帝时，从车骑将军朱雋征黄巾，为别部司马。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Ling he followed chariot-and-horse general Zhu Jun to campaign against the Yellow Turbans as separate-column major.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ling he served Zhu Jun against the Yellow Turbans as major of a detached column.

sentences.zh: 著赋、颂、碑文、荐、檄、笺、书、谒文、嘲，凡十九篇。

translations.literal: He authored fu, odes, stelae, recommendations, proclamations, notes, letters, visiting texts, and jeers—nineteen pieces in all.
translations.idiomatic: His rhapsodies, hymns, inscriptions, recommendations, manifestos, notes, letters, calling cards, and lampoons number nineteen.

sentences.zh: 超又善于草书，妙绝时人，世共传之。

translations.literal: Chao was also skilled in cursive script, subtle beyond his contemporaries; the age together transmitted copies.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at cursive hand, unmatched in his day, and copyists spread his sheets.

sentences.zh: 祢衡字正平，平原般人也。

translations.literal: Mi Heng, courtesy name Zhengping, was a man of Bo in Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Heng, courtesy name Zhengping, was from Bo in Pingyuan commandery.

sentences.zh: 少有才辩，而尚气刚傲，好矫时慢物。

translations.literal: In youth he had talent and disputation, yet prized spirit, was stubborn and proud, loved to correct the age and slight things.
translations.idiomatic: Young, he was brilliant and disputatious, proud of temper, fond of defying fashion and sneering at the great.

sentences.zh: 兴平中，避难荆州。

translations.literal: In the Xingping years he fled trouble to Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Xingping he took refuge in Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 建安初，来游许下。

translations.literal: At the start of Jian'an he came wandering to Xu below.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jian'an he drifted to Xu.

sentences.zh: 始达颍川，乃阴怀一剌，既而无所之适，至于刺字漫灭。

translations.literal: When first he reached Yingchuan he secretly carried one visiting card; afterward there was nowhere suitable to go, until the card's lettering wore away.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Yingchuan he tucked a single name card in his sleeve, found no door worth knocking, until the ink wore off.

sentences.zh: 是时，许都新建，贤士大夫，四方来集。

translations.literal: At that time the new capital at Xu was first built; worthy gentlemen and great officers gathered from the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Xu was new-built then, and talent flocked from every quarter.

sentences.zh: 或问衡曰：“盍从陈长文、司马伯达乎？

translations.literal: Someone asked Heng: "Why not follow Chen Zhangwen and Sima Boda?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone said: "Why not call on Chen Qun or Sima Lang?"

sentences.zh: ”对曰：“吾焉能从屠沽兒耶！

translations.literal: He replied: "How could I follow butcher and wine-boy lads!"
translations.idiomatic: He snapped: "Am I to trail tavern brats?"

sentences.zh: ”又问：“荀文若、赵稚长云何？

translations.literal: " Again they asked: "What of Xun Wenruo and Zhao Zhichang?"
translations.idiomatic: They asked next: "What of Xun Yu and Zhao Yan?"

sentences.zh: ”衡曰：“文若可借面吊丧，稚长可使监厨请客。

translations.literal: " Heng said: "Wenruo could lend a face for mourning visits; Zhichang could supervise the kitchen and invite guests."
translations.idiomatic: Mi Heng said: "Xun Yu has a face fit only for borrowed mourning calls; Zhao Yan could keep the kitchen and pour the wine."

sentences.zh: ”唯善鲁国孔融及弘农杨脩。

translations.literal: " Only Lu's Kong Rong and Hongnong's Yang Xiu won his praise.
translations.idiomatic: Only Kong Rong of Lu and Yang Xiu of Hongnong earned his respect.

sentences.zh: 常称曰：“大兒孔文举，小兒杨德祖。

translations.literal: He constantly declared: "The elder son is Kong Wenju; the younger is Yang Dezu.
translations.idiomatic: He called them "the great lad Kong Wenju, the lesser Yang Dezu."

sentences.zh: 余子碌碌，莫足数也。

translations.literal: The rest are mediocrities—not worth counting."
translations.idiomatic: The others were hacks—not worth reckoning."

sentences.zh: ”融亦深爱其才。

translations.literal: " Rong also deeply loved his talent.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Rong loved his gifts in return.

sentences.zh: 衡始弱冠，而融年四十，遂与为交友。

translations.literal: Heng had just reached the weak-crown years while Rong was forty; thereupon they became friends.
translations.idiomatic: Mi was barely twenty, Kong forty, yet they became sworn friends.

sentences.zh: 上疏荐之曰：

translations.literal: Rong submitted a memorial recommending him, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Kong Rong then memorialized the throne:

sentences.zh: 臣闻洪水横流，帝思俾乂，旁求四方，以招贤俊。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that when the flood waters rampaged, the emperor thought of helpers, searched the four quarters, to summon worthy men.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that when the Deluge raged, the sage sought helpers everywhere.

sentences.zh: 昔孝武继统，将弘祖业，畴咨熙载，群士响臻。

translations.literal: Formerly Filial Wu continued the line, wished to enlarge the ancestral enterprise, inquired far and wide for shining service, and gentlemen flocked like echoes.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu widened the Han line, asked the realm for shining talent, and worthies answered in hosts.

sentences.zh: 陛下睿圣，纂承基绪，遭遇厄运，劳谦日昃。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is sagely and wise, inheriting the foundation, meeting evil times, toiling in modesty from sun to sun.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, sage and wise, took up the torch in dark days and toils humbly dawn to dusk.

sentences.zh: 惟岳降神，异人并出。

translations.literal: The marchmount sends down its spirit; strange men appear together.
translations.idiomatic: The sacred peak breathes forth spirit; rare men rise at once.

sentences.zh: 窃见处士平原祢衡，年二十四，字正平，淑质贞亮，英才卓砾。

translations.literal: Privately I have seen the reclusive gentleman Mi Heng of Pingyuan, age twenty-four, courtesy name Zhengping—pure substance, bright faith, outstanding genius.
translations.idiomatic: I note the recluse Mi Heng of Pingyuan, twenty-four, style Zhengping—clear in character, blazing in talent.

sentences.zh: 初涉艺文，升堂睹奥。

translations.literal: First treading letters and arts, he mounted the hall and glimpsed the inner chamber.
translations.idiomatic: First steps in letters took him straight to the inner room of learning.

sentences.zh: 目所一见，辄诵于口；

translations.literal: What his eye once saw, at once he could chant from the mouth;
translations.idiomatic: What his eye skimmed his tongue could repeat;

sentences.zh: 耳所瞥闻，不忘于心。

translations.literal: what his ear briefly heard, did not leave his heart.
translations.idiomatic: what his ear caught his mind would not lose.

sentences.zh: 性与道合，思若有神。

translations.literal: Nature matches the Way; his thought seems spiritlike.
translations.idiomatic: His nature meets the Dao; his thought seems almost divine.

sentences.zh: 弘羊潜计，安世默识，以衡准之，诚不足怪。

translations.literal: Sang Hongyang's hidden reckoning, Zhang Anshi's silent memory—set Heng beside them and it is hardly strange.
translations.idiomatic: Sang Hongyang's silent sums, Zhang Anshi's wordless recall—Mi Heng matches them without strain.

sentences.zh: 忠果正直，志怀霜雪。

translations.literal: Loyal, decisive, upright—his will holds frost and snow.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal, blunt, straight—his purpose is ice and snow.

sentences.zh: 见善若惊，疾恶若仇。

translations.literal: He marvels at good as if startled, hates evil as if an enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He starts at the sight of good, hunts evil like a foe.

sentences.zh: 任座抗行，史鱼厉节，殆无以过也。

translations.literal: Ren Zuo's defiant conduct, Shi Yu's fierce integrity—probably nothing surpasses him.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Zuo's blunt courage, the historian Yu's steel—none outdoes him.

sentences.zh: 鸷鸟累伯，不如一鹗。

translations.literal: A flock of hawks piled high is not worth one osprey.
translations.idiomatic: A mob of kites is worth less than one sea-eagle.

sentences.zh: 使衡立朝，必有可观。

translations.literal: If Heng were set in court, there would surely be something worth seeing.
translations.idiomatic: Set him in the hall and the court would have something to see.

sentences.zh: 飞辩骋辞，溢气坌涌，解疑释结，临敌有余。

translations.literal: Flying disputation, racing phrases—breath overflows and surges; he unties doubts and loosens knots, facing foes with plenty to spare.
translations.idiomatic: His wit races, his breath boils—he untangles riddles and still has force for the foe.

sentences.zh: 昔贾谊求试属国，诡系单于；

translations.literal: Formerly Jia Yi begged trial as dependent-state clerk, swore to bind the Chanyu;
translations.idiomatic: Jia Yi asked to try office on the frontier, swore to rope the Chanyu;

sentences.zh: 终军欲以长缨，牵致劲越。

translations.literal: Zhong Jun wished with a long cord to drag in mighty Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Jun vowed a long cord to haul in southern Yue.

sentences.zh: 弱冠慷慨，前世美之。

translations.literal: Weak-crown age, high mettle—the former age praised them.
translations.idiomatic: Young heroes—past ages sang their praise.

sentences.zh: 近日路粹、严象，亦用异才，擢拜台郎，衡宜与为比。

translations.literal: Recently Lu Cui and Yan Xiang also by unusual talent were promoted to terrace gentlemen—Heng ought to be ranked with them.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Cui and Yan Xiang rose by rare gifts to terrace posts—Mi Heng belongs in their company.

sentences.zh: 如得龙跃天衢，振翼云汉，扬声紫微，垂光虹蜺，足以昭近署之多士，增四门之穆穆。

translations.literal: If he may leap like a dragon on heaven's highway, beat wings in the Milky Way, raise voice in the Purple Palace, trail light like a rainbow—enough to display the many scholars of your near bureau, increase the four gates' solemn awe.
translations.idiomatic: Let him vault the sky road like a dragon, beat wings in the River of Stars, thunder in the Purple Palace, trail rainbow light—then your inner court will show its wealth of talent and the four gates grow grave with awe.

sentences.zh: 钧天广乐，必有奇丽之观；

translations.literal: In the Kunlun heavens' vast music there must be marvelous, splendid sights;
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's great symphony must hold wonders never seen;

sentences.zh: 帝室皇居，必蓄非常之宝。

translations.literal: the imperial house and royal dwelling surely stores extraordinary treasures."
translations.idiomatic: the royal house surely hoards gems beyond price."

sentences.zh: 若衡等辈，不可多得。

translations.literal: Men such as Heng cannot be gotten in abundance.
translations.idiomatic: Men like Mi Heng do not come twice in an age.

sentences.zh: 《激楚》、《杨阿》，至妙之容，台牧者之所贪；

translations.literal: "Rushing Chu" and "Yang'e"—supreme beauty of form—what terrace shepherds covet;
translations.idiomatic: "Rushing Chu" and "Yang'e"—the acme of grace—what every governor craves;

sentences.zh: 飞兔、騕褭，绝足奔放，良、乐之所急。

translations.literal: Flying Rabbit, Yaoniao—matchless hooves at the gallop—what Bo Le urgently seeks.
translations.idiomatic: Flying Rabbit, Yaoniao—steeds no rein can hold—what Bo Le would give his eye for.

sentences.zh: 臣等区区，敢不以闻。

translations.literal: We, your petty subjects, dare not fail to report.
translations.idiomatic: We humbly dare not keep this from your ears.

sentences.zh: 融既爱衡才，数称述于曹操。

translations.literal: Rong already loved Heng's talent and repeatedly praised him to Cao Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Rong loved his genius and praised him again and again to Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 操欲见之，而衡素相轻疾，自称狂病，不肯往，而数有恣言。

translations.literal: Cao wished to see him, but Heng had always despised him with hatred, called himself mad and refused to go, and repeatedly uttered reckless words.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao wished to meet him, but Mi Heng had long despised him, pleaded madness, stayed away, and kept pouring out insults.

sentences.zh: 操怀忿，而以其才名，不欲杀之。

translations.literal: Cao harbored resentment, yet because of his talent and name, did not wish to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Cao nursed a grudge yet spared him for fear of ruining his own name.

sentences.zh: 闻衡善击鼓，乃召为鼓史，因大会宾客，阅试音节。

translations.literal: Hearing that Heng was good at beating drums, he summoned him as drum clerk and, because of a great assembly of guests, reviewed and tested rhythm and pitch.
translations.idiomatic: Learning Mi Heng was a master drummer, he named him drum clerk and, at a great banquet, made him prove his skill.

sentences.zh: 诸史过者，皆令脱其故衣，更着岑牟、单绞之服。

translations.literal: All clerks who passed were ordered to strip their old clothes and put on pointed caps and single-layer crossed robes.
translations.idiomatic: Every drummer had to strip and don the clown cap and motley wrap.

sentences.zh: 次至衡，衡方为《渔阳》参挝，蹀□而前，容态有异，声节悲壮，听者莫不慷慨。

translations.literal: When it came to Heng, Heng was just performing the "Yuyang" triple beat, mincing steps forward; his bearing was strange, the sound and rhythm tragic and bold—listeners none failed to be stirred.
translations.idiomatic: When Mi Heng's turn came he struck the "Yuyang" roll, strutting forward with a wild air, the beat fierce and mournful—every guest sat upright.

sentences.zh: 衡进至操前而止，吏呵之曰：“鼓史何不改装，而轻敢进乎？

translations.literal: Heng advanced to before Cao and stopped; clerks shouted at him: "Drum clerk, why do you not change dress—how dare you lightly advance?"
translations.idiomatic: He halted before Cao Cao; aides barked: "Why have you not changed costume, drummer?"

sentences.zh: ”衡曰：“诺。

translations.literal: " Heng said: "Yes."
translations.idiomatic: "Very well," said Mi Heng.

sentences.zh: ”于是先解衵衣，次释余服，裸身而立，徐取岑牟、单绞而着之，毕，复参挝而去，颜色不怍。

translations.literal: " Thereupon first he removed his inner shirt, next shed the remaining garments, stood naked, slowly took the pointed cap and single crossed robe and put them on; finished, again performed the triple beat and departed, his color not ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: He peeled off his shirt, shed the rest, stood naked, then slowly donned cap and motley, finished the roll, and walked off without a blush.

sentences.zh: 操笑曰：“本欲辱衡，衡反辱孤。

translations.literal: Cao laughed, saying: "Originally I wished to shame Heng—Heng instead shamed me.
translations.idiomatic: Cao laughed: "I meant to humble him—he humbled me."

sentences.zh: 孔融退而数之曰：“正平大雅，固当尔邪？

translations.literal: Kong Rong withdrew and rebuked him, saying: "Zhengping, great refinement—should it indeed be thus?"
translations.idiomatic: Kong Rong took him aside: "Zhengping—was this worthy of you?"

sentences.zh: ”因宣操区区之意。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he announced Cao's petty intent.
translations.idiomatic: He relayed Cao Cao's small-minded terms.

sentences.zh: 衡许往。

translations.literal: Heng promised to go.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Heng agreed to call.

sentences.zh: 融复见操，说衡狂疾，今求得自谢。

translations.literal: Rong again saw Cao, explaining that Heng's mad illness now sought to apologize in person.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Rong told Cao the "madness" had passed and Mi would apologize.

sentences.zh: 操喜，敕门者有客便通，待之极晏。

translations.literal: Cao was pleased, ordered gatekeepers whenever there was a guest then admit, and waited for him extremely late.
translations.idiomatic: Cao was pleased, told the gate to pass any visitor, and waited till very late.

sentences.zh: 衡乃着布单衣、疏巾，手持三尺棁杖，坐大营门，以杖捶地大骂。

translations.literal: Heng then wore plain cloth single robe, loose headcloth, in hand held a three-chi club, sat at the great camp gate, and with the club beat the earth and reviled loudly.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Heng came in thin robe and kerchief, a three-foot baton in hand, sat at the camp gate, and drummed the ground with curses.

sentences.zh: 吏曰：“外有狂生，坐于营门，言语悖逆，请收案罪。

translations.literal: Clerks said: "Outside there is a mad student sitting at the camp gate; his words are contrary and rebellious—please seize and try him for crime."
translations.idiomatic: Guards reported: "A madman sits at the gate, shouting treason—arrest him."

sentences.zh: ”操怒，谓融曰：“祢衡竖子，孤杀之犹雀鼠耳。

translations.literal: " Cao was angry and said to Rong: "Mi Heng is a brat—for me to kill him is still like sparrow or mouse."
translations.idiomatic: Cao snarled to Kong Rong: "That whelp Mi Heng—I could crush him like a bug."

sentences.zh: 顾此人素有虚名，远近将谓孤不能容之，今送与刘表，视当何如。

translations.literal: Only this man has long had empty fame; far and near will say I cannot tolerate him—now I send him to Liu Biao and see how it will be."
translations.idiomatic: Yet he has a famous name; if I kill him the world will call me narrow—pack him off to Liu Biao instead."

sentences.zh: ”于是遣人骑送之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he sent men mounted to escort him.
translations.idiomatic: He had him escorted south by horse.

sentences.zh: 临发，众人为之祖道，先供设于城南，乃更相戒曰：“祢衡勃虐无礼，今因其后到，咸当以不起折之也。

translations.literal: When about to depart, the crowd for him performed the road rite, first setting out provisions south of the city; then they mutually warned: "Mi Heng is brutal and rude without rites—now because he comes late, all should by not rising humble him."
translations.idiomatic: Friends gathered south of the city to see him off and agreed: "Mi Heng is insufferable—when he comes late we will all stay seated to humble him."

sentences.zh: ”及衡至，众人莫肯兴，衡坐而大号。

translations.literal: " When Heng arrived, the crowd none would rise; Heng sat and gave a great wail.
translations.idiomatic: When he came no one stood; Mi Heng sat down and burst into a wail.

sentences.zh: 众问其故，衡曰：“坐者为冢，卧者为尸。

translations.literal: The crowd asked the reason; Heng said: "Those who sit are tombs; those who lie are corpses.
translations.idiomatic: They asked why; he said: "Seated guests are burial mounds; those who sprawl are corpses.

sentences.zh: 尸冢之间，能不悲乎！

translations.literal: Between corpse and tomb—how can one not grieve!"
translations.idiomatic: Between tomb and corpse—should I not weep?"

sentences.zh: 刘表及荆州士大夫，先服其才名，甚宾礼之，文章言议，非衡不定。

translations.literal: Liu Biao and the Jingzhou gentlemen, beforehand impressed by his talent and name, treated him very much as guest of honor; documents and discussions, without Heng, were not settled.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao and the Jingzhou scholars, awed by his fame, honored him as chief guest—no memorial passed without his polish.

sentences.zh: 表尝与诸文人共草章奏，并极其才思。

translations.literal: Biao once with various men of letters jointly drafted a memorial, together exhausting their talent and thought.
translations.idiomatic: Once Liu Biao and his writers drafted a joint memorial, straining every wit.

sentences.zh: 时衡出，还见之，开省未周，因毁以抵地。

translations.literal: At the time Heng went out; returning he saw it, opened and examined it not completely, therefore tore it and dashed it to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Heng stepped out; on return he skimmed the draft, tore it up, and flung it down.

sentences.zh: 表怃然为骇。

translations.literal: Biao was blank and startled.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao gaped, stunned.

sentences.zh: 衡乃从求笔札，须臾立成，辞义可观。

translations.literal: Heng then from him sought brush and slips; in a moment he finished, phrasing and meaning admirable.
translations.idiomatic: He demanded brush and paper, and in moments produced a new text, phrasing and sense superb.

sentences.zh: 表大悦，益重之。

translations.literal: Biao was greatly pleased and esteemed him the more.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao was delighted and prized him higher.

sentences.zh: 后复侮慢于表，表耻，不能容，以江夏太守黄祖性急，故送衡与之，祖亦善待焉。

translations.literal: Later again he insulted and slighted Biao; Biao felt shame and could not contain him—because Jiangxia grand warden Huang Zu was hasty of temper, therefore he sent Heng to him; Zu likewise treated him well.
translations.idiomatic: Later he insulted Liu Biao, who could not stomach the shame—knowing Huang Zu of Jiangxia was quick-tempered, he palmed Mi Heng off on him; Huang Zu welcomed him kindly.

sentences.zh: 衡为作书记，轻重疏密，各得体宜。

translations.literal: Heng for him did secretary work—weight and lightness, density and spacing, each obtained what was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: As his secretary Mi Heng gauged every tone—light or heavy, tight or loose—perfectly.

sentences.zh: 祖持其手曰：“处士，此正得祖意，如祖腹中之所欲言也。

translations.literal: Zu grasped his hand, saying: "Recluse, this just hits Zu's intent—as what Zu would wish to speak from within the belly."
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zu clasped his hand: "Sir, this is exactly what I meant—words drawn from my own belly."

sentences.zh: 祖长子射，为章陵太守，尤善于衡。

translations.literal: Zu's eldest son She was grand warden of Zhangling and was especially good to Heng.
translations.idiomatic: Huang She, Huang Zu's heir as Zhangling grand warden, loved him best.

sentences.zh: 尝与衡俱游，共读蔡邕所作碑文，射爱其辞，还恨不缮写。

translations.literal: Once he and Heng together roamed, together read a stele inscription by Cai Yong; She loved its phrasing, returning regretted not having copied it.
translations.idiomatic: They once read a Cai Yong inscription together; Huang She loved the text but had no copy.

sentences.zh: 衡曰：“吾虽一览，犹能识之，唯其中石缺二字，为不明耳。

translations.literal: " Heng said: "Though I once glanced at it, still I can remember it—only in the middle the stone lacks two characters—not clear."
translations.idiomatic: Mi Heng said: "One reading was enough—only two characters on the stone are chipped away."

sentences.zh: ”因书出之，躬驰使写碑，还校，如衡所书，莫不叹伏。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he wrote it out, personally sent a runner to copy the stele, returned and collated—it matched what Heng had written; none failed to sigh in submission.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote it from memory; Huang She sent a man to the stone—the copy matched; all marveled.

sentences.zh: 射时大会宾客，人有献鹦鹉者，射举卮于衡曰：“愿先生赋之，以娱嘉宾。

translations.literal: She at the time held a great assembly of guests; someone presented a parrot; She raised a cup toward Heng: "I hope, sir, you will compose a fu on it to entertain the noble guests."
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet someone brought a parrot; Huang She raised his cup: "Sir, please compose a rhapsody to delight our guests."

sentences.zh: ”衡揽笔而作，文无加点，辞采甚丽。

translations.literal: " Heng grasped the brush and composed; the text had no dotting corrections, phrasing and color very lovely.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Heng took brush and wrote at once—no blot, no erasure, the lines gorgeous.

sentences.zh: 后黄祖在蒙冲船上，大会宾客，而衡言不逊顺，祖惭，乃呵之。

translations.literal: Later Huang Zu on a covered-strike boat held a great assembly of guests, but Heng's speech was not deferent; Zu felt shame and therefore shouted at him.
translations.idiomatic: Later, on a war-boat banquet, Mi Heng spoke rudely; Huang Zu, embarrassed, barked at him.

sentences.zh: 衡更熟视曰：“死公！

translations.literal: Heng stared harder and said: "Dead old man!"
translations.idiomatic: Mi Heng glared: "You dead dotard!"

sentences.zh: 云等道？

translations.literal: What talk is that?
translations.idiomatic: What filth is that from your mouth?

sentences.zh: ”祖大怒，令五百将出，欲加箠。

translations.literal: " Zu was greatly angry, ordered the five hundred guards to lead him out, wishing to apply the rod.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zu roared for the guards to drag him out for a beating.

sentences.zh: 衡方大骂，祖恚，遂令杀之。

translations.literal: Heng was meanwhile reviling loudly; Zu in fury thereupon ordered him killed.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Heng kept cursing; Huang Zu, in a fury, ordered him slain.

sentences.zh: 祖主簿素疾衡，即时杀焉。

translations.literal: Zu's chief clerk had always hated Heng; at once he killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The chief clerk, who loathed him, struck at once.

sentences.zh: 射徒跣来救，不及。

translations.literal: She came barefoot to save him, but did not reach in time.
translations.idiomatic: Huang She ran barefoot to stop it—too late.

sentences.zh: 祖亦悔之，乃厚加棺敛。

translations.literal: Zu also regretted it, then richly supplied coffin and shroud.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zu repented and buried him with honor.

sentences.zh: 衡时年二十六，其文章多亡云。

translations.literal: Heng at the time was twenty-six sui; much of his writing is lost, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: He was twenty-six; most of his writings are lost.

sentences.zh: 赞曰：情志既动，篇辞为贵。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Once feeling and intent move, pieces and phrasing are precious.
translations.idiomatic: The verdict runs: When heart stirs, the word is the jewel.

sentences.zh: 抽心呈貌，非雕非蔚。

translations.literal: Drawing out the heart, displaying the form—neither carve nor overgrow.
translations.idiomatic: Lay bare the heart, show the face—neither carve nor smother.

sentences.zh: 殊状共体，同声异气。

translations.literal: Strange shapes share one body; same tone, different breath.
translations.idiomatic: Many shapes, one frame; one song, many winds.

sentences.zh: 言观丽则，永监淫费。

translations.literal: In speech observe the fair pattern; forever mirror against excess.
translations.idiomatic: Read the lovely pattern—and forever guard against wanton waste.
